Invests in(Preseed, Seed, Series A ...): Seed (Surge), Series A, Series B+, Growth
Company Thesis: Full-stack partner backing founders from seed to IPO across India and Southeast Asia; build enduring companies, increasingly AI-focused.
Sector: AI, SaaS, FinTech, Consumer Internet, Enterprise, Developer Tools
Cheque Size: Surge seed up to $3M; Series A ~$8–16M; larger growth cheques
Notes: Independent since 2023 Sequoia split. ~$9B AUM across 13 funds; 440+ cos, 39 unicorns, 26+ IPOs (Zomato, Meesho, Groww, Wakefit). Raised ~$1.3B in 2026. Runs Surge (170+ startups). Led by Shailendra Singh.
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Peak XV Partners is the leading venture and growth firm across India and Southeast Asia, operating independently since its 2023 separation from Sequoia Capital. It manages roughly $9 billion across 13 funds and has backed over 440 companies in 19 years, producing 39 unicorns and more than two dozen public listings, including Zomato, Meesho, Groww and Wakefit. In early 2026 it raised about $1.3 billion across three vehicles — an India seed fund, an India venture fund and an APAC fund — with most capital earmarked for India. Peak XV runs a full-stack model spanning seed to pre-IPO. Its Surge program (launched 2019) gives early-stage founders up to $3 million in seed capital plus company-building workshops and a global operator community; over 170 startups and 400+ founders have gone through it. Series A cheques typically range $8–16 million, with deep follow-on reserves for winners. The team of ~89, including 16 partners across Bengaluru and Singapore, is led by Shailendra Singh and is increasingly focused on AI and cross-border opportunities. With one of Asia's largest portfolios and an integrated seed-to-IPO platform, Peak XV remains the default institutional partner for the region's most ambitious technology founders.

Invests in(Preseed, Seed, Series A ...): Seed, Series A (+ Series B follow-on)
Company Thesis: Back the unknown Indian entrepreneur poised to become tomorrow's global leader; partner early with technology and tech-enabled founders and lead rounds, nurturing them across the growth journey.
Sector: Consumer, Enterprise/SaaS, FinTech, Retail, HealthTech, DeepTech
Cheque Size: $500K–$5M (Seed avg ~$2.2M, Series A avg ~$4.85M); prefers to lead
Notes: Bengaluru. Founded 2006 as Indo-US Venture Partners (NEA partnership); rebranded Kalaari 2012. Founders Vani Kola & Vinod Dham. ~$650M AUM, 157 cos, 8 unicorns, 3 IPOs, 31 acquisitions. Portfolio: Myntra, Cult.fit, BlueStone, Digantara. Team 29 incl 11 partners.
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Kalaari Capital is one of India's pioneering early-stage technology venture firms, founded in 2006 by Vani Kola and Vinod Dham as Indo-US Venture Partners — a partnership with NEA — and rebranded as Kalaari in 2012. Headquartered in Bengaluru, it manages approximately $650 million across its funds and is led by Managing Director Vani Kola, who spent 22 years building and exiting technology companies in Silicon Valley before returning to India. That operator-turned-investor perspective shapes Kalaari's founder-first, mentorship-led approach. The firm invests primarily at seed and Series A, writing cheques of roughly $500K to $5 million, and prefers to lead rounds while reserving capital for follow-on participation; average seed rounds run about $2.2 million and Series A near $4.85 million. Across 19 years it has backed around 157 companies, producing 8 unicorns, 3 IPOs and 31 acquisitions, with notable names including Myntra, Cult.fit, BlueStone and, more recently, space-data startup Digantara. Its team of 29, including 11 partners, spans technology, consumer, fintech and operations expertise. Beyond capital, Kalaari operates as a thought-leadership and community engine, offering portfolio companies structured playbooks and domain knowledge. The firm is also a champion of first-time and diverse founders, reflecting Kola's philosophy of recognising and scaling ambitious early entrepreneurs.

Invests in(Preseed, Seed, Series A ...): Inception, Seed, Series A (+ Series B follow-on)
Company Thesis: Back extraordinary founders building product-first companies that redefine categories across the world's two largest startup ecosystems — the US and India; be the first institutional investor and partner from day one.
Sector: AI, Enterprise Software & Infrastructure, Consumer, FinTech, Vertical SaaS, Commerce
Cheque Size: $500K–$10M; prefers first institutional cheque and a board seat
Notes: Founded 2006. HQ Menlo Park + Bengaluru/Mumbai. ~$3.2B AUM across 11 funds; Fund VIII $700M (Dec 2025, largest global VC fund of 2025), Fund VII $700M (2023). 130+ active cos, 16 unicorns, 11 IPOs. Portfolio: Delhivery, Postman, Zepto, Rapido, Infra.Market, Turtlemint. GPs: Suvir Sujan, Anup Gupta (India); Jishnu Bhattacharjee, Abhishek Sharma (US).
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Nexus Venture Partners is a pioneering cross-border venture capital firm built specifically around the two largest startup ecosystems in the world — the United States and India. Founded in 2006, it operates from Menlo Park alongside Bengaluru and Mumbai, and manages roughly $3.2 billion across eleven funds. In December 2025 it closed its eighth fund at $700 million — described as the largest venture fund raised globally that year — deliberately splitting capital between US-based AI investments and India-focused opportunities; its seventh fund (2023) was also $700 million. Nexus typically acts as the first institutional investor at inception, seed and Series A, writing cheques from about $500K to $10 million, taking a board seat, and reserving capital for follow-on rounds. Its focus spans AI, enterprise software and infrastructure, consumer technology, fintech and commerce. Across nearly 20 years it has backed more than 130 active companies, producing 16 unicorns and 11 IPOs, including Delhivery, Postman, Zepto, Rapido, Infra.Market and Turtlemint, and has returned significant liquidity through exits such as Delhivery, PubMatic, MapmyIndia and Unicommerce. The firm — led by general partners Suvir Sujan and Anup Gupta in India and Jishnu Bhattacharjee and Abhishek Sharma in the US — encourages Indian portfolio companies to establish US operations early, bridging talent and capital across both markets.

Company Thesis: First-cheque angel backing disruptive early-stage founders across India and the US; plays the power law — focus on the magnitude of a few outsized successes rather than frequency, holding 3–5 years for outcomes.
Sector: FinTech, Consumer, SaaS, Crypto/Blockchain, SpaceTech, Enterprise
Cheque Size: Personal angel cheques (small first cheques); via 100X.VC uses iSAFE notes (~INR 25 lakh / ~$30–50K)
Notes: Mumbai. Angel since 2011; 150–230+ personal investments. Founder/Partner 100X.VC (SEBI AIF, sponsored by Mehta Ventures family office). 4 unicorns: OYO (280x exit), CoinDCX, Block.One, AXIOM Space. Portfolio: OYO, Wow! Momo, Box8, LogiNext, Unbxd, PrettySecrets, Coolberg, InstaSafe.
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Sanjay Mehta is among the most prolific and successful angel investors in India, a Mumbai-based serial entrepreneur who has been a first-cheque backer of early-stage startups since 2011. Before investing, he founded MAIA Intelligence, later acquired by Datamatics. Across his personal career he has backed somewhere between 150 and 230+ startups in India and the US, and is widely cited as the only Indian angel with four unicorns to his name: OYO, crypto exchange CoinDCX, blockchain company Block.One, and US space-infrastructure firm AXIOM Space. His most celebrated outcome was a roughly 280x return from an early OYO position; a partial exit from Block.One returned several thousand percent in under three years. Mehta articulates a power-law philosophy — that a small fraction of a portfolio drives almost all returns, so investors should optimise for the magnitude of success, not its frequency, and be patient across three-to-five-year horizons. In December 2019 he institutionalised this approach by founding 100X.VC, India's first fund to invest using iSAFE (India SAFE) notes, sponsored by his Mehta Ventures family office, with an ambition to back 100 startups a year. Notable portfolio names include OYO, Wow! Momo, Box8, LogiNext, Unbxd, PrettySecrets, Coolberg and InstaSafe. He is also a prominent blogger and ecosystem thought leader.

Company Thesis: Founder-angel backing consumer-internet and fintech businesses that leverage trust, data and distribution to reshape Indian markets; brings deep behavioural-economics insight and strong ecosystem signalling.
Sector: FinTech, Consumer Internet, SaaS, Commerce, Marketplaces
Cheque Size: Individual angel cheques (typically undisclosed; often part of a syndicate/consortium)
Notes: Founder of CRED (2018) and FreeCharge (acquired by Snapdeal). One of India's most prolific founder-investors: 260–290+ startups backed, ~11–13 unicorns. Portfolio: Razorpay, Unacademy, Spinny, Slice, BharatPe, Khatabook, Zetwork, Shiprocket, Nothing (Carl Pei). Board: CRED, Happay, Pine Labs; advisor to Y Combinator and Peak XV.
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Kunal Shah is one of India's most influential entrepreneurs and its single most prolific founder-turned-angel investor. He first built FreeCharge, a digital payments and recharge platform later acquired by Snapdeal, before founding CRED in 2018 — a fintech platform rewarding creditworthy users that has grown into one of the country's most prominent unicorns. His personal wealth, largely tied to his CRED stake, is estimated around $500–600 million. As an angel, Shah has backed more than 260 startups across India and the US — the largest such portfolio of any Indian founder-investor — of which roughly a dozen have become unicorns. His investments span Razorpay, Unacademy, Spinny, Slice, BharatPe, Khatabook, Zetwork, Shiprocket and even Carl Pei's consumer-electronics venture Nothing, reflecting a thesis rooted in consumer internet, fintech and trust-and-distribution-driven businesses. Shah is known for sharp, contrarian thinking grounded in behavioural economics, frequently shared with a large public following, and his participation in a round carries strong signalling value in the ecosystem. Beyond writing cheques, he holds board seats at CRED, Happay and Pine Labs and has advised Y Combinator and Peak XV (Sequoia India). His blend of operator credibility, network depth and brand equity makes him a highly sought-after early backer for India's most ambitious consumer and fintech founders.

Company Type: Angel Investor / VC (Managing Partner, Celesta Capital)
Company Thesis: Back product-led founders building across the India–US corridor, drawing on two decades of operating experience at global platforms to help with product, GTM and cross-border scaling.
Notes: Ex-CPO/product leader at Five9, Meta (Messenger), Bharti Airtel, Snapdeal/FreeCharge; founder of Aeroprise (acq. BMC). 80+ angel investments, ~10 unicorns; ranked #1 India–US seed investor by Hurun 2022–24. Former Partner at General Catalyst (built India–US practice); now Managing Partner, Celesta Capital; co-founded Crescendo & HiOctave. Portfolio: MoEngage, Rupeek, DealShare, NoBroker, FPL/OneCard, Exotel, Scaler, SAFE Security.
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Anand Chandrasekaran is one of the most recognised angel investors operating across the India–US technology corridor, and a seasoned product executive. Over two decades he served as a product leader at Five9 — where he helped grow revenue from roughly $120M to $600M ARR — Meta's Messenger Platform, Bharti Airtel and Snapdeal/FreeCharge, and earlier founded Aeroprise, acquired by BMC Software. Since 2015 he has made more than 80 angel investments, around ten of which have become unicorns, and was ranked the #1 seed investor focused on the India–US corridor by the Hurun India report for three consecutive years (2022–2024). His portfolio spans enterprise software, AI, fintech and consumer, including MoEngage, Rupeek, DealShare, NoBroker, FPL Technologies (OneCard), Exotel, Scaler and SAFE Security. He brings a distinctive operator's lens to early-stage investing — deep product intuition and a global network — helping founders with product strategy, go-to-market and cross-border expansion. After establishing the India–US investing practice as a Partner at General Catalyst, where he also co-created the AI-first contact-centre company Crescendo, he is now Managing Partner at Celesta Capital, a deep-tech focused firm, while continuing to back founders. A Stanford graduate, he was named a World Economic Forum Young Global Leader and to Fortune India's 40-under-40.

Invests in(Preseed, Seed, Series A ...): Pre-Seed, Seed, Pre-Series A / Series A
Company Thesis: Back passionate, driven founders early across consumer tech, fintech, SaaS, consumer brands, healthtech and B2B services; lead seed rounds and double down on winners through later rounds.
Sector: Consumer Tech, FinTech, SaaS, Consumer Brands, HealthTech, B2B Services
Cheque Size: ~$300K–$500K seed lead (Titan Seed Fund, proprietary); follow-on ~INR 15 Cr avg via Winners Fund
Notes: Co-founder of Snapdeal & AceVector (also Unicommerce, Stellaro Brands); Shark Tank India S4 judge. Titan Capital (with Rohit Bansal) investing since 2011: 250–280+ startups. Winners Fund = SEBI Cat-II AIF, ₹333 Cr final close (2024), follow-on into ~20 winners. Portfolio: Ola, Urban Company, Razorpay, Mamaearth, OfBusiness, Unicommerce, Credgenics.
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Kunal Bahl is a pioneering Indian technology entrepreneur and one of the country's most active founder-investors. He co-founded Snapdeal in 2010 with Rohit Bansal, building it into one of India's largest e-commerce platforms, and today chairs AceVector, the holding company for Snapdeal, Unicommerce and Stellaro Brands. Alongside Bansal he runs Titan Capital, an early-stage investment firm through which the pair have backed more than 250–280 startups since 2011 — initially entirely from their own capital. Titan Capital is sector-agnostic but emphasises passionate, driven founders across consumer tech, fintech, SaaS, consumer brands, healthtech and B2B services, typically leading seed rounds with cheques of roughly $300K–$500K through its proprietary Titan Seed Fund. Its portfolio includes some of India's biggest successes — Ola, Urban Company, Razorpay, Mamaearth, OfBusiness, Unicommerce and Credgenics. In 2024 the firm raised external capital for the first time via the Titan Capital Winners Fund, a SEBI Category-II AIF that closed at ₹333 crore and is dedicated to follow-on investments in around 20 of its best-performing portfolio companies at an average ticket of about ₹15 crore. A judge on Shark Tank India and a member of the National Startup Advisory Council, Bahl is among the most influential voices in Indian entrepreneurship.

Company Thesis: Back passionate founders with disruptive ideas in early-stage technology, drawing on edtech and consumer-internet operating experience to mentor on product and scaling.
Sector: EdTech, Consumer Tech, SaaS, Media & Entertainment, Enterprise, Gaming
Notes: Co-founder & CEO of Unacademy (founded 2015, edtech unicorn, peaked ~$3.4B). Earlier founded Flatchat (acq. CommonFloor 2014); also Graphy, Airlearn. Angel in ~48–63 startups across India & US. Portfolio: Pine Labs, Pratilipi, Ultrahuman, Rheo TV, TapChief, Lissun, Gully Labs.
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Gaurav Munjal is the co-founder and CEO of Unacademy, one of India's largest online learning platforms, and an active early-stage angel investor. He began as a technologist and entrepreneur, founding the student-accommodation app Flatchat (acquired by CommonFloor in 2014) before building Unacademy — which started as a YouTube channel in 2010 and was formally founded in 2015 with Roman Saini, Hemesh Singh and Sumit Jain. Under his leadership Unacademy grew into an edtech unicorn, reaching a peak valuation of roughly $3.4 billion after a 2020 SoftBank-led round, and he has since steered it toward profitability while also launching ventures like Graphy and Airlearn. As an angel, Munjal has backed somewhere between 48 and 63 startups across India and the US, spanning edtech, consumer technology, SaaS, media and entertainment, enterprise software and gaming. His portfolio includes Pine Labs, Pratilipi, Ultrahuman, Rheo TV, TapChief, Lissun and Gully Labs. He typically invests at pre-seed and seed and is known for backing founders with strong conviction and product clarity, offering mentorship on scaling consumer products in emerging markets. As one of India's most prominent edtech founders and a vocal advocate for its startup ecosystem, his backing carries meaningful signalling value for early-stage founders.

Company Thesis: Make value-add, operationally-oriented investments in companies with proven unit economics, ~20% YoY growth and $1–10M revenue, partnering with high-repute entrepreneurs building long-lasting businesses.
Sector: Consumer, Technology, Leisure Infrastructure, Software, Media & Entertainment, FinTech, Retail
Notes: Founder/CEO of OYO. Personal vehicle Aroa Ventures (Singapore, est. 2020), sponsored by RACo Holding, 100% controlled by Agarwal, headed by Gaurav Gulati (ex-Innov8 COO). ~₹418 Cr AUM, ~45 investments. Portfolio: ZipLoan, Fashalot, Atomberg, GIFSKEY, Wysh, Shyle. Also Shark Tank India guest investor.
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Ritesh Agarwal is the founder and CEO of OYO, the SoftBank-backed global hospitality company, and one of India's youngest self-made billionaires. He channels his personal investing through Aroa Ventures, a Singapore-based firm he established in 2020, sponsored by his RACo Holding Company and fully controlled by him, with day-to-day operations led by Gaurav Gulati, the former COO of Innov8 (which OYO acquired in 2019). Aroa focuses on early and growth-stage businesses across consumer, technology and leisure-infrastructure sectors, and is explicitly operationally oriented — seeking companies with proven unit economics, roughly 20% year-on-year growth and $1–10 million in annual revenue, run by high-repute entrepreneurs building long-lasting businesses. The firm writes cheques between $500K and $5 million (about ₹4–41 crore) and, beyond capital, helps portfolio companies accelerate growth and improve risk-adjusted returns. Aroa manages around ₹418 crore and has made roughly 45 investments, with sector exposure spanning software, media and entertainment, finance and retail; named portfolio companies include ZipLoan, Fashalot, Atomberg Technologies, GIFSKEY, Wysh and, via Shark Tank India, Shyle. Agarwal's scaling experience across 80-plus countries gives him a distinctive global operating perspective on unit economics, distribution and expansion that founders value alongside his capital and brand.

Company Thesis: Back scalable, innovative solutions to real-life problems across tech and consumer/D2C; an operator-investor who mentors founders on building and scaling, with a sharp eye on unit economics.
Sector: Consumer Internet, D2C, FinTech, E-commerce, SaaS, DeepTech, CleanTech, HealthTech, Mobile
Notes: Founder/CEO People Group (Shaadi.com, Makaan.com, Mauj Mobile). Angel since 2007 (first: Interactive Avenues). 200–250+ startups; Shark Tank India judge S1–S3. Portfolio: Ola, BigBasket, Rapido, Rupeek, Druva, Agnikul, FarEye, NxtWave, Animall, Whatfix, plus D2C (Skippi, Hair Originals). Ticket researched: typical first cheque $50K–$500K (Pipeseed); historically ~₹25–50L average with larger outliers (Business Today).
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Anupam Mittal is one of India's most recognisable entrepreneurs and prolific angel investors, best known as the founder and CEO of Shaadi.com — among the world's largest matrimonial platforms — and of People Group, which also operates Makaan.com and Mauj Mobile, India's first mobile-gaming and value-added-services company. Born in Mumbai in 1971 and educated at Boston College, he pioneered internet-based consumer services in India from the late 1990s. He began angel investing in 2007 with Interactive Avenues (a digital advertising agency that became his most successful early bet) and has since backed more than 200–250 startups across consumer internet, D2C, fintech, e-commerce, SaaS, deep tech, clean tech and healthcare. His portfolio includes Ola, BigBasket, Rapido, Rupeek, Druva, Agnikul, FarEye, NxtWave, Animall and Whatfix, alongside numerous D2C brands such as Skippi and Hair Originals. Mittal reached a far wider audience as a judge on Shark Tank India across its first three seasons, where he invested roughly ₹1.89 crore across 55-plus businesses and became known for sharp questioning around unit economics, founder credibility and defensibility. His investment philosophy centres on backing scalable, innovative solutions to real problems, and his blend of operator credibility, capital and mass-media visibility makes him a high-signal early backer.

Company Thesis: India's largest early-stage investment platform: combine a pan-India angel community with SEBI-registered funds to back early-stage tech founders — including first-generation founders in Tier-II/III cities — with capital plus deep mentorship.
Sector: AI/ML, DeepTech, Biotech, FinTech, Consumer, HealthTech, SpaceTech, MSME
Cheque Size: Angel collaborative ~INR 1.2 Cr ($0.14M) avg; larger via IAN Alpha Fund
Notes: Now IAN Group (founded 2006). Funds: IAN Angel Fund (evergreen), IAN Alpha Fund (SEBI Cat-II, $100M/INR 900 Cr final close Dec 2025), BioAngels. 225+ portfolio cos, 3 unicorns; catalysed ~INR 18,000 Cr. Leadership: Padmaja Ruparel (co-founder), Chintan Thakkar (Group CEO, ex-Info Edge), Vinod Keni, Priyank Garg. Portfolio: Druva, Spinny, Uniphore, FarEye, Zypp Electric.
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Indian Angel Network — now IAN Group — is India's largest and one of its oldest early-stage investment platforms, founded in 2006. It pairs a pan-India community of angel investors with a family of SEBI-registered venture funds, giving founders both capital and deep operator mentorship. The platform has built a portfolio of more than 225 companies, including three unicorns, and claims to have catalysed roughly INR 18,000 crore of follow-on investment and helped create tens of thousands of jobs. Its structure spans the evergreen IAN Angel Fund, the BioAngels vertical, and the IAN Alpha Fund — a SEBI Category-II vehicle that marked its final close at $100 million (about INR 900 crore) in December 2025, with a notable share of investments in first-generation founders across Tier-II and Tier-III cities. Collaborative angel cheques average around INR 1.2 crore, with larger amounts deployed through the Alpha Fund and top-ups into existing portfolio companies. IAN invests across AI/ML, deep tech, biotech, fintech, consumer, healthtech, spacetech and the MSME category. Its leadership includes co-founder Padmaja Ruparel and Group CEO Chintan Thakkar (former Info Edge CFO), alongside Vinod Keni and Priyank Garg. Portfolio names include Druva, Spinny, Uniphore, FarEye, Zypp Electric and Manastu Space.

Company Thesis: 'Founder-only' approach — be the first significant backer at pre-seed when conviction matters more than metrics; decide in 7 days, wire within 30, then partner seed-to-IPO. Sector-agnostic, leaning Consumer (D2C/B2C) and SaaS/GenAI.
Notes: Gurugram. Founded 2024 by solo GP Bipin Shah (IIT Bombay; ex-Partner/MD Titan Capital; 14 yrs early-stage, evaluated ~50,000 startups, met 5,000+ founders, backed 250+). Fund I INR 159 Cr (~$18M), final close Oct 2025, 3.5x oversubscribed; 52% from 31 founder-LPs incl 18 unicorn founders (e.g. Aman Gupta/boAt). Portfolio: Gully Labs, Frex, Supply 6, SteamPRO. Past bets (via Titan): Mamaearth, Credgenics, InVideo, Giva, CityMall; exits Beardo, Oziva, SuprDaily. | Ticket researched: Cheque size ₹1–6 Cr (~$120K–$720K) (VCCircle / Moneycontrol)
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Zeropearl VC is a solo-GP, pre-seed and seed-stage micro-fund founded in 2024 and based in Gurugram, established by Bipin Shah — an IIT Bombay alumnus and former partner/managing director at Titan Capital with over 14 years in early-stage investing. Shah's personal track record is among the most prolific in India: he has evaluated more than 50,000 startups, met thousands of founders, and backed 250-plus ventures, with early bets on Mamaearth, Credgenics, InVideo, Giva and CityMall, and exits including Beardo (acquired by Marico), Oziva (HUL) and SuprDaily (Swiggy). Zeropearl closed its maiden fund at INR 159 crore (about $18 million) in October 2025, oversubscribed more than 3.5 times against an INR 80 crore target before being capped to retain selectivity; notably, 52% of the corpus came from 31 founder-LPs, including 18 unicorn founders such as boAt's Aman Gupta, who provide operational mentorship and network access alongside capital. The fund follows a distinctive 'founder-only' philosophy — aiming to be the first significant backer at the friends-and-family or pre-seed stage — and a rapid, conviction-led process: a yes-or-no answer within seven days and funds wired within 30. It is sector-agnostic with a lean toward consumer (D2C/B2C) and SaaS/GenAI, targets roughly 8% ownership, and plans to back around 45 startups, guiding them toward a strong Series A within 15 months. Portfolio names include Gully Labs, Frex and Supply 6.

Invests in(Preseed, Seed, Series A ...): Series A, Series B, Growth Equity, Buyouts, Public Markets
Company Thesis: Evergreen, crossover capital backing emerging and disruptive technologies and category-leading companies with enduring value built to thrive in public markets; returns primarily support the Azim Premji Foundation.
Sector: Technology, Consumer, Financial Services, Healthcare, Industrials
Cheque Size: Historically ~$20–60M; $100M+ for late-stage (early-stage practice does Series A/B)
Notes: Family office of Azim Premji (Wipro), founded 2006, Bengaluru + US. Multi-billion-dollar AUM across private (early/growth/buyout) and public markets. 124+ cos, 27 unicorns. Team ~84 incl 19 partners. Portfolio: Flipkart, Purplle, LambdaTest, GIVA, The Sleep Company, KreditBee, Dezerv. Returns fund Azim Premji Foundation.
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Premji Invest is the investment arm of Azim Premji, founder of Wipro, and one of India's most significant and distinctive capital allocators. Founded in 2006 and headquartered in Bengaluru with a US presence, it operates as an evergreen, crossover firm investing across both private and public markets — spanning early-stage (Series A and B), growth equity, buyouts and public equities — with a multi-billion-dollar asset base. Its focus areas are technology, consumer, financial services, healthcare and industrials, and it is known for patient, long-duration capital rather than fixed fund cycles. A defining feature is its purpose: the returns Premji Invest generates primarily fund the Azim Premji Foundation, a non-profit working to improve the lives of India's underserved. The firm has backed more than 120 companies, including 27 unicorns, with named investments such as Flipkart, Purplle, LambdaTest, GIVA, The Sleep Company, KreditBee and Dezerv, and it frequently co-invests with global institutions like BlackRock. Late-stage cheques have historically run in the $20–60 million range, rising to $100 million-plus, while a dedicated early-stage practice partners with Series A/B teams building global companies with public-market ambitions. With a team of around 84 including 19 partners, Premji Invest's backing is widely regarded as a strong signal of company quality and governance.

Company Thesis: Back early-stage, technology-focused founders building defensible IP with a clear path to profitability; Fund III is ~80% focused on deep-tech, semiconductor, space and defence.
Sector: Deep-tech, Semiconductor, SpaceTech, DefenceTech, SaaS, FinTech, ClimateTech, AgriTech
Notes: Founded 2015 by Bhaskar Majumdar & Anil Joshi (Mumbai). 3 funds; Fund III ~INR 1,200 Cr. Portfolio 60+ incl. Open (unicorn), Sequretek, Genrobotics, Pharmarack, SmartCoin, EyeROV, OrbitAID.
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Unicorn India Ventures (UIV) is a Mumbai-based, SEBI-registered early-stage venture fund founded in 2015 by Bhaskar Majumdar and Anil Joshi. It invests as the first institutional cheque in technology-focused founders building defensible intellectual property with a clear path to profitability, and is deliberately contrarian — avoiding hype-driven sectors. Across three funds UIV has built an active portfolio of more than 60 companies, including its neobanking unicorn Open, plus Sequretek, Genrobotics, Pharmarack, SmartCoin, EyeROV and OrbitAID, and has seen multiple acquisitions. Its third fund, closing near INR 1,200 crore, marks a sharp pivot toward deep technology: roughly 80% of capital is earmarked for semiconductor design, space and defence, alongside SaaS, fintech, climate-tech and agritech. UIV typically writes initial cheques of around $1–2 million (about INR 10 crore) and reserves substantial follow-on capital — up to $10–15 million — for its strongest companies, deploying only a portion of the corpus initially and concentrating reserves on winners. Fund III's limited partners are split roughly evenly between international investors, domestic institutions, and Indian family offices and UHNIs. The founders bring an unusual blend of media, corporate and angel-network experience, and Anil Joshi is known for candid, governance-focused mentorship of founders.

Company Thesis: Invest in early-stage disruptive startups 'building the India of tomorrow', combining technology with impact; integrity- and trust-led, long-term partnerships over quick wins. Deliberately avoids me-too consumer brands, generic SaaS and fintech.
Sector: DeepTech, Robotics, Drones, IoT, Hardware, AI applications (Agri/Climate/Health), B2B/Enterprise SaaS, Blockchain
Notes: Mumbai. Founded 2022 by Suresh Jain (ex-Networth; founder Sun Capital/Sun Global; 3+ decades in capital markets) with children Saloni Jain & Darshan Jain as founding partners. Backed by an industrial family-office network. Maiden fund closed. Portfolio: Suind (drones), Dhiway (blockchain), Omnivio, AjnaLens, CultYvate, Vidyakul.
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Sun Icon Ventures is a Mumbai-based early-stage venture capital fund founded in 2022 by capital-markets veteran Suresh Jain, alongside his children Saloni and Darshan Jain as founding partners. Jain spent decades on the sell-side — exiting Networth after the 2008 crisis to build Sun Capital and Sun Global — before transitioning to the buy-side with Sun Icon, backed by a multi-decade industrial family-office network. The firm invests in early-stage disruptive startups 'building the India of tomorrow', combining technology with measurable impact, and is explicitly values-driven: Jain emphasises integrity and trust as non-negotiables and favours long-term partnerships over quick wins, looking beyond pitch decks to founders' intent and character. Sun Icon writes cheques of roughly $30K to $400K at seed to pre-Series A, with the ability to lead or co-lead and target ownership of 1–15%, supported by senior/technical hiring help, Series A intros and a manufacturing, supply-chain and distribution network. Its interests centre on AI-driven solutions in agriculture, climate and healthcare, plus robotics, drones, IoT, hardware and B2B/enterprise SaaS. Notably, it consciously avoids marketing-heavy consumer brands, saturated generic SaaS and the crowded, tightly-regulated fintech sector. Portfolio companies include drone startup Suind, blockchain firm Dhiway, Omnivio, AjnaLens, agritech CultYvate and vernacular e-learning platform Vidyakul.

Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Neon Fund is an early-stage venture firm built specifically to help Indian B2B SaaS and enterprise-AI startups go global, founded by Siddhartha Ahluwalia and Nansi Mishra — hosts of the widely followed Neon Show (formerly the 100x Entrepreneur podcast). The fund is structured as a Delaware limited partnership operating across the US and India, and its LP base includes CXOs from Amazon, Microsoft and HP, plus prominent SaaS founders and investors like Blume Founders Fund and Nexus's Sandeep Singhal. Recent portfolio companies include Requestly (acquired by BrowserStack), Highperformr, Zepic and Merlin AI. About half its bets back second-time founders, the rest first-timers with strong revenue focus.

Fund I closed at roughly INR 76–80 crore ($9.5 million) and backed 23 startups, of which several have crossed $1 million ARR with 8x revenue growth. Fund II, launched in September 2023 with a target of INR 450 crore, reached a final close of INR 255 crore backed by family offices, HNIs and entrepreneurs across India and the US, and aims to back 16–25 companies. Ticket sizes run from about INR 75 lakh to INR 3 crore at pre-seed to Series A in Fund I, rising to roughly INR 4–8 crore in Fund II. Portfolio companies include OneStack, Vodex, ElevateHQ, AyushPay, Kenko Health, TurboHire, Riskcovry and ShopSe. Beyond capital, Pentathlon offers deep enterprise networks and operator mentorship.

Company Thesis: India-focused healthcare and wellness fund investing exclusively in scalable companies with validated product-market fit, governance-aligned leadership and a clear pathway to institutional scale; sector specialisation plus long-term partnership capital.

Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Alkemi Growth Capital is a New Delhi-based, early-growth venture fund focused exclusively on India's healthcare and consumer-wellness sectors, founded in 2017 by Alka Goel, who returned from the US to launch one of the few women-led venture funds in the country. Alongside partner Dr. Mansi Aggarwal and a team drawn from McKinsey, IIM-Ahmedabad and AIIMS, Goel has built Alkemi into a sector-specialist investor backing scalable companies that have validated product-market fit, governance-aligned leadership and a clear pathway to institutional scale. The firm's debut fund holds roughly $34 million in assets and has made around 20 investments, primarily at Series A, with cheque sizes spanning $100K to $5 million and a sweet spot near $1.5 million. It is now raising a second fund targeting $75 million, having reached a first close of about $49.7 million with the IFC committing up to $10 million in equity plus a co-investment envelope — a strong endorsement of its strategy and ESG framework. Portfolio companies include diagnostics chain Redcliffe Labs, healthy-snacking brand Farmley, healthcare-staffing platform Jobizo and Akiva Superfoods, with an exit in Doxper. Alkemi's advisory board features senior healthcare and business leaders, including the CEOs of Medanta, Cipla and Swiggy, reinforcing its operator and clinical network.

Company Thesis: Accelerate Indian new-age consumer brands — helping micro-businesses and product/brand owners grow reach across online and offline retail via an omni-channel approach, plus fundraising support; enters at the product-market-fit stage.

Its stated mission is to help micro-businesses, product makers and D2C brand owners 'go from zero to one' — entering at the product-market-fit stage and accelerating growth by expanding a brand's reach across both online channels and physical retail through an omni-channel distribution approach, while also supporting founders in raising capital. The firm is run by first-generation founders and operators with hands-on experience in the consumer-goods sector, including a D2C toy-and-gifting business; one founding partner also established Rowboat, a community launched in 2022 that connects founders and investors. WEIN positions itself around speed, low cost and growth for the brands it backs, and frames the next decade as 'India's decade' for consumer entrepreneurship. Public disclosure on the firm is currently limited — fund size, typical cheque size and a named portfolio are not publicly available — so this profile is intentionally conservative and will be expanded as verified details emerge. Company Thesis: Founders-led, sector-agnostic technology micro-VC backing high-quality teams identified through 'green signals'; bridge India's business heritage — family offices and second-generation entrepreneurs — with future-forward startups, offering networks, GTM and hiring help beyond capital.

Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Warmup Ventures is a Jaipur-based, founders-led micro-VC firm that began in mid-2023 as a syndicate before scaling into an institutional fund. Sector-agnostic but technology-focused, it invests at pre-seed and seed, placing particular emphasis on 'green signals' that indicate high-quality founding teams. The firm's partners — a team of around ten including four partners — have themselves walked the founder's path of scaling businesses, raising capital and building teams, and they position Warmup as more than a cheque: portfolio companies get help with introductions to follow-on investors, connections to CEOs of large tech companies for business synergies, go-to-market planning and key technical hires. A distinctive part of its thesis is bridging India's traditional business heritage with its innovation economy by connecting family offices and second-generation entrepreneurs with future-forward startups. In December 2024 Warmup launched a ₹300 crore second fund, aiming to deploy roughly ₹5–7 crore into each of 25–30 early-stage startups with reserves for follow-on rounds. It has backed more than fifteen companies to date, including bubble-tea chain Bobabhai (expanded to 45 stores), Nitro Commerce, agri-equipment brand Balwaan Krishi, battery-recycling startup MiniMines, RocketPay and industrial-IoT platform DATOMS, with several having gone on to raise larger rounds — evidence of its early-conviction model.

Company Thesis: Partner with global teams on a mission to solve the world's most important problems; founder-first, impact-oriented investing with gender-lens principles, prioritising defensible IP and scalable models.

Notes: Mumbai. Founded 2017 by Paula Mariwala — one of India's first women VCs, founder of Stanford Angels & Entrepreneurs India, ex-MD Seedfund. Co-founders incl. A Stanford-educated physicist and technologist, Mariwala has been shaping the country's startup ecosystem since 2006 — she is the founder and President Emeritus of Stanford Angels & Entrepreneurs India, the former Managing Director of Seedfund (one of India's first venture funds), and a promoter director of the Hinditron Group. Aureolis partners with global teams on a mission to solve significant problems, focusing on climate change, health, deep tech, education and consumer, and invests across pre-seed, seed and Series A. The firm takes a founder-first, impact-oriented approach and is an active participant in gender-lens investing, looking beyond female founders to companies whose products and workplaces benefit women. Its portfolio spans 49 companies, including the unicorn Unacademy, alongside agritech firm Fasal, warehouse-robotics company Unbox Robotics and digital-health platform Zyla Health. Mariwala's broader 25-year investing career includes notable exits such as RedBus, Carwale and TapChief, giving her deep experience across the full venture lifecycle from sourcing to exit. Backed by a small, hands-on team of around twelve including co-founders Jo Pattabiraman and Ruchi Jain Hanasoge, Aureolis offers portfolio founders close mentorship and access to global networks to help them scale with impact.

Company Thesis: India's first domestic consumer-centric fund — 'invest in the Consumer of Tomorrow, Today'; back first-generation entrepreneurs disrupting large, sticky consumer categories with differentiated skill sets rather than just capital.

Headquartered in Mumbai, Sixth Sense has grown to over $150 million in assets under management across two funds, with around 23 investments and a reported IRR near 40%. Its first fund (SSIO I) raised INR 118 crore, while its second (SSIO II) closed at INR 515 crore — more than double its INR 250 crore target — in a record nine months; both funds have been ranked among the top five Indian venture firms of the past decade by Preqin. The fund typically invests $1–5 million per company across consumer, FMCG, retail, D2C and food and beverage. Its portfolio includes Bombay Shaving Company, Cult.fit, Purplle, Wonderchef, luxury-watch retailer ETHOS, INDICOLD and Bewakoof. Beyond capital, Sixth Sense leverages a deep consumer ecosystem — distribution, branding and FMCG networks — to help founders scale, making it the preferred partner for consumer businesses in India.

Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Disruptors Capital is a founder-dedicated, early-stage venture capital fund based across New Delhi and Bengaluru (with a US presence), founded in 2021 by Raj Snehil Juneja. Juneja came to investing from the advisory side — having worked with around 500 startups and run fundraising and M&A transactions at Khetal Advisors — and built Disruptors after observing that strong founders often struggle to raise institutional rounds because of structural gaps and a lack of early guidance. The firm secured SEBI approval in early 2022 to launch a ₹120 crore Category-I Alternative Investment Fund, which invests in technology startups across India, South-East Asia and the US Bay Area. Beyond capital, Disruptors leans on the experience of seasoned operators — including fund partner Krishna Kumar, CEO of Simplilearn — to help portfolio founders refine business models, sharpen product thinking and build go-to-market strategies. While rooted in India, 8X leverages close relationships across the Middle East and Europe to help portfolio companies expand internationally and attract regional investors for larger follow-on rounds. Portfolio companies include robotics-and-sanitation innovator Solinas Integrity, Pantherun, Xyma Analytics, LightSpeed Photonics and Enerzi.

Its maiden fund is sized at around ₹100 crore (roughly $12–15 million), with a plan to back about 30 startups in 18 months at ₹1–6 crore per deal and support them through exits typically targeted within three to five years; the firm has since launched a much larger deep-tech vehicle, the SilverX Fund, reportedly around ₹800 crore. These collaborations can take varied forms, including strategic investments, strategic acquisitions, joint ventures, technology licensing, and manufacturing and distribution agreements. Precog works with 15-plus innovation-led ecosystems across the US, Europe, Southeast Asia, ANZ, Canada and Israel, and provides ventures with strategic access to capital, talent, distribution networks and manufacturing and supply-chain support to enter and scale in the Indian market. Its portfolio spans around 16 companies — with air-purification firm AirOK Technologies among the most notable — and it has recorded outcomes including an IPO and two acquisitions across names such as Linkker, Emuron and Climate Connect.
