Company Type: VC (early-stage / Pre-Series A, DeepTech & B2B; SEBI AIF)
Company Thesis: Nurture global market leaders from India by backing product-led, IP-backed DeepTech and enterprise (B2B) founders; a horizontal partnership model with a high partner-to-founder ratio, concentrating efforts on a handful of companies for long-term success.
Sector: DeepTech (AI, IoT, Robotics, SpaceTech, Quantum, AR/VR/MR, Edge Cloud, HealthTech), B2B Enterprise/SaaS
Cheque Size: Early-stage / Pre-Series A cheques (Fund III $69M across ~20–25 startups)
Notes: Gurugram. Founded 2011 by Sunil K Goyal (MD & Fund Manager; partners incl. Girish Shivani, Sanjay Pande). Three funds: Fund I (2012, $14M/INR 90 Cr, 16 cos; exits Uniphore, SmartQ; returned ~70% of corpus); Fund II (2017, $30M/INR 215 Cr, 19 DeepTech cos — Miko, Dozee, Exponent Energy); Fund III ($69M, anchored by sovereign fund NIIF). Cumulative AUM ~$53M valued ~$1.2bn (May 2025). 58 cos, 1 unicorn (Uniphore), 9 acquisitions.
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): YourNest Venture Capital is a Gurugram-based, early-stage fund established in 2011 to nurture global market leaders from India, led by Managing Director and Fund Manager Sunil K Goyal. Sharply focused on the 'Pre-Series A' stage, it backs product-led, IP-backed startups in DeepTech — spanning AI, IoT, robotics, space tech, quantum computing, AR/VR/MR, edge cloud and health tech — alongside enterprise (B2B) software. The firm has built a thesis around India's shift from an IT-services outsourcing hub to an IP- and patent-driven 'Product Nation', and operates a distinctive horizontal partnership model with a high partner-to-founder ratio, deliberately investing in a small number of founders and concentrating its efforts on each. YourNest has launched three funds roughly every five years: Fund I (2012, ~$14M, 16 companies, with exits including Uniphore and SmartQ returning much of the corpus); Fund II (2017, ~$30M/₹215 crore, 19 deep-tech startups such as Miko, Dozee and Exponent Energy); and Fund III, a ~$69M vehicle anchored by India's sovereign National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF). Its three funds carry a cumulative AUM of about $53 million valued near $1.2 billion as of May 2025, across 58 companies that include one unicorn — conversational-AI leader Uniphore — and nine acquisitions, with the firm targeting ₹2,000 crore in AUM over the next three years.

Company: Venture Catalysts | India's First Integrated Incubator
Company Type: Integrated Incubator + Angel Network / Multi-stage VC (VCats Group)
Invests in(Preseed, Seed, Series A ...): Pre-Seed, Seed, Early-stage (+ follow-on via group funds)
Company Thesis: India's first integrated incubator — combine capital, mentoring and network to write early external cheques for nascent startups; syndicate deals with HNIs, family offices and CXOs, and provide ~3 months of acceleration plus ~18 months of post-investment support.
Sector: Sector-agnostic (FinTech, Consumer/D2C, EV & Mobility, AI/ML, Retail/FMCG, AR/VR)
Notes: Mumbai. Founded 2015 by Apoorv Ranjan Sharma, Anuj Golecha, Anil Jain & Gaurav Jain. India's first & largest integrated incubator/angel network; 10,000+ angels & family offices; present across 31 Indian cities + UAE, US, UK, Singapore; curates 600+ deals/month. Flagship accelerator fund: 100Unicorns (formerly 9Unicorns). Portfolio: BharatPe, Fynd, Beardo, Pee Safe, Klub, Shiprocket, Zypp Electric, BluSmart, Niyo. 45+ global co-investors; 35+ multibagger exits.
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Venture Catalysts is India's first and largest integrated incubator and angel network, founded in 2015 by Apoorv Ranjan Sharma, Anuj Golecha, Anil Jain and Gaurav Jain, and headquartered in Mumbai. It pioneered a model that combines capital, mentoring and network on a single platform — pooling money from a community of more than 10,000 angel investors, HNIs and family offices to write early external cheques for nascent startups. The firm typically invests $275K to $2 million in early-stage companies through syndicated rounds, and provides every portfolio company roughly three months of acceleration support followed by around 18 months of post-investment guidance, with scope for follow-on cheques of ₹3–5 crore for those showing sustained promise. Venture Catalysts curates more than 600 deals a month and operates across 31 Indian cities and four countries (UAE, US, UK and Singapore). Its flagship accelerator fund, 100Unicorns (formerly 9Unicorns), institutionalises idea-stage seed capital at scale. The group's portfolio includes category leaders such as BharatPe, Fynd, Beardo, Pee Safe, Klub, Shiprocket, Zypp Electric, BluSmart and Niyo, and it has attracted more than 45 international Grade-A co-investors — including Google, Accel, Sequoia, Bain Capital and Y Combinator — while delivering 35-plus multibagger exits over five years.

Company Thesis: Invest to improve access to sustainable energy and resource-productivity solutions for the underserved in India; back solutions that drive inclusive development and build communities resilient to climate change, starting small and growing alongside portfolio companies with hands-on, operator-first support.
Sector: CleanTech, Energy Tech, Climate, Environment Tech, Food & Agriculture Tech
Notes: Gurugram/New Delhi (Chattarpur). Founded 2016 (entity since 2012) by Karthik Chandrasekar (IIT-Bombay; ex-TVS Capital, Ventureast, Acumen). ~19–20 investments, 50+ deals; team ~35 incl 13 partners. Portfolio: Inficold, Promethean Energy, Smart Joules, Cell Propulsion, Carbon Masters/Carbonlites. Runs AIC Sangam (CleanTech incubator with Atal Innovation Mission). Network/LPs incl. IFC, Aavishkaar, GIZ, Bharat Innovation Fund. | Ticket researched: Seed/early $100K–$2M (Venture Capital Archive)
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Sangam Ventures is a seed and early-stage venture fund based in Gurugram/New Delhi, founded by Karthik Chandrasekar, who developed his interest in climate and cleantech during his B.Tech years at IIT-Bombay and learned venture investing at TVS Capital Funds, Ventureast and the impact fund Acumen before starting Sangam around 2016. The fund's mission is to improve access to sustainable energy and resource-productivity solutions for the underserved in India, backing solutions that drive inclusive development and build communities resilient to climate change. Its focus spans cleantech, energy tech, climate and environment tech, and food and agriculture tech. Reflecting Chandrasekar's Acumen-shaped philosophy that early-stage entrepreneurship needs 'something beyond the money', Sangam takes a hands-on, operator-first approach, deliberately starting with small cheques and growing alongside its portfolio companies — appropriate for cleantech businesses that don't require large capital at inception. The firm has made around 19–20 investments across 50-plus deals, supported by a team of roughly 35 including 13 partners, with notable portfolio companies including thermal-battery cooling firm Inficold, Promethean Energy, energy-efficiency company Smart Joules, Cell Propulsion and Carbon Masters. Sangam also runs AIC Sangam, a cleantech incubator in partnership with the Atal Innovation Mission, and counts IFC, Aavishkaar, GIZ and Bharat Innovation Fund among its ecosystem partners.

Company Type: VC (deep-tech thematic, SEBI Cat-I AIF; part of CIIE.CO / IIM Ahmedabad)
Invests in(Preseed, Seed, Series A ...): Seed to Series B (Pre-Series A / Series A core)
Company Thesis: Back IP-driven deep-tech founders building 'companies of consequence' that remain outside most VCs' deal flow at inception; as high-touch investors, lead founders in the right direction and help de-risk technology, regulatory and execution risk over long gestation periods, providing network, customers and resources.
Sector: DeepTech / IP-led — AI, AR/VR, IoT, ML, Big Data; HealthTech, AgriTech, Renewable Energy, FinTech infrastructure
Cheque Size: Initially INR 3–15 Cr (BIF); INR 2–6 Cr (Bharat Inclusion Seed Fund)
Notes: Ahmedabad. Founded 2018 under CIIE.CO at IIM Ahmedabad; co-founder Ashwin Raguraman (earlier India Innovation Fund, 2010). $100M corpus split across Bharat Innovation Fund + Bharat Inclusion Seed Fund. 27 investments; 1 unicorn (CRED), 2 acquisitions (Setu, Prefr). Portfolio: PlayShifu, Entropik Tech, CreditVidya, Detect Technologies, vPhrase, Portl, Optimized Electrotech, Virohan. LPs incl. SIDBI FoF, ICICI Lombard, SBI Life, RBL Bank, Federal Bank. Fund II planned.
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Bharat Innovation Fund (BIF) is an Ahmedabad-based, deep-tech-focused venture firm launched in 2018 under the aegis of CIIE.CO, the Centre for Innovation, Incubation and Entrepreneurship continuum at IIM Ahmedabad, and co-founded by Ashwin Raguraman, who had earlier run the India Innovation Fund. A SEBI Category-I AIF with a $100 million corpus — allocated across BIF and the sister Bharat Inclusion Seed Fund — it was created specifically to back IP-driven deep-tech and breakthrough-innovation startups that typically fall outside most VCs' profiles and deal flow at the earliest stages, where the first product is expensive and slow to build. BIF invests across Seed to Series B, with initial cheques generally between ₹3 and ₹15 crore, in sectors spanning AI, AR/VR, IoT, machine learning and big data applied to healthcare, agriculture, renewable energy and advanced technology; the Inclusion Seed Fund writes ₹2–6 crore into India-Stack-based products for the next billion users. As high-touch investors, the team focuses on de-risking technology, regulatory and execution challenges over long gestation cycles. Its portfolio of around 27 companies includes PlayShifu, Entropik Tech, CreditVidya, Detect Technologies, Portl, Optimized Electrotech and Virohan, with one unicorn (CRED) and acquisitions in Setu and Prefr. Its institutional LPs include SIDBI's Fund of Funds, ICICI Lombard, SBI Life, RBL Bank and Federal Bank, and a second fund is planned.

Invests in(Preseed, Seed, Series A ...): Seed, Series A (up to Series B)
Company Thesis: Back entrepreneurs building breakthrough technologies for agriculture, food, climate and the rural economy that deliver disproportionate impact on the lives of farmers and rural communities in India and Southeast Asia; conviction that Indian agritech companies are 'built to last'.
Sector: AgriTech, FoodTech, ClimateTech, Rural Economy — farmer platforms, agri-fintech, precision agriculture, F2C brands, post-harvest/supply chain, agrifood life sciences
Cheque Size: $1–5M initial (Fund III); seed avg ~$2.6M, Series A ~$5.7M
Notes: Mumbai. Founded 2010 by Mark Kahn & Jinesh Shah — India's first dedicated agritech VC; partners Reihem Roy & Subhadeep Sanyal; team ~18 incl 4–5 partners. Three funds + ACSF; cumulative AUM ~$700M+. Fund III (Agritech & Climate Sustainability Fund) first close $150M (launched Apr 2022), 25–30 investments planned. 57–59 cos, 5 exits. Portfolio: DeHaat, Ecozen, Pixxel, Stellapps, Varaha, Tractor Junction, Loopworm. DFI LPs: IFC, KfW, FMO, Proparco, Gates Foundation, Louis Dreyfus, Yara, SIFEM, SRI Fund.
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Omnivore is India's pioneering agrifood and climate-focused impact venture firm, founded in 2010 in Mumbai by Mark Kahn and Jinesh Shah as the country's first dedicated agritech VC — Kahn having previously been EVP of Strategy and Business Development at Godrej Agrovet. Alongside partners Reihem Roy and Subhadeep Sanyal and an 18-person team, Omnivore backs early-stage founders building breakthrough technologies across farmer platforms, agri-fintech, precision agriculture, farm-to-consumer brands, post-harvest and supply-chain tech, and agrifood life sciences, investing across seed to Series A (occasionally Series B) in India and Southeast Asia. The firm has built roughly $700 million in cumulative AUM across three funds plus its Agritech & Climate Sustainability Fund. Its third fund reached a first close of $150 million in 2023 (launched April 2022), backed by a deep development-finance LP base including IFC, KfW, FMO, Proparco, SIFEM, the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, Louis Dreyfus Company Ventures and Yara Growth Ventures, and plans 25–30 new investments at initial cheques of roughly $1–5 million, with a sharper focus on life sciences and climate resilience. Across 57-plus investments and five exits, its portfolio includes DeHaat, climate-smart deeptech firm Ecozen, space-tech company Pixxel, dairy-tech firm Stellapps, carbon-removal startup Varaha and Tractor Junction — collectively touching over 12 million smallholder farmers.

Company Thesis: Fuel the economic resilience of underserved low-income customers and 'Entrepreneurial Households' by investing at the intersection of inclusivity, affordability and scale; deliver measurable impact alongside financial returns via the proprietary 'Elevar Method'.
Sector: FinTech / Financial Inclusion, Education, Healthcare, Agri-supply chains, MSME & Housing
Notes: Bengaluru (+US). Founded 2008. Leadership: Johanna Posada (Founder & MP), Jyotsna Krishnan (MP), partners Vipul Rawal, Amie Patel, Shobha Venkataraman; team ~29 incl 8 partners. 5 funds, ~$400M AUM; Fund V (Elevar India V) target $225M (first close $126M), SME-focused. 47–56 investments; 3 unicorns, 2 IPOs (Ujjivan SFB, Bharat Financial Inclusion), 9 acquisitions. Impacted 50M+ households, ~70,000 jobs, 20M women borrowers. Portfolio: Ujjivan SFB, InCred, Varthana, Aye Finance, TapFin, Hippo Stores. Cross-border (India + LatAm).
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Elevar Equity is a Bengaluru-headquartered impact venture firm, founded in 2008, that invests at the intersection of inclusivity, affordability and scale to fuel the economic resilience of underserved low-income customers and what it calls 'Entrepreneurial Households'. Over a 15-plus-year journey it has raised five funds, manages roughly $400 million in AUM, and has catalysed billions in follow-on capital while serving more than 50 million households — supporting around 70,000 jobs and providing loans to some 20 million women borrowers. Its investment themes span financial inclusion, education, healthcare, agri-supply chains and MSME solutions, typically at seed to Series A. The firm's latest vehicle, Elevar India V, targets $225 million and reached a first close of about $126 million, backed by development-finance investors such as British International Investment, focusing on early-stage SMEs delivering essential goods and services. Led by Founder and Managing Partner Johanna Posada and Managing Partner Jyotsna Krishnan, with a 29-person team including eight partners, Elevar applies its proprietary 'Elevar Method' to back businesses serving marginalised customers. Across roughly 56 investments it has produced three unicorns, two IPOs — notably Ujjivan Small Finance Bank and Bharat Financial Inclusion — and nine acquisitions, with portfolio names including InCred, Varthana, Aye Finance, TapFin and Hippo Stores; the firm also invests across India and Latin America.

Company Thesis: Collaborate with future change-makers to build and scale impact startups; a curated accelerator program designed to bring the best out of seed to pre-series startups, backing 'revolutionary founders building from Bharat to the world' with capital, mentorship and operational support.
Sector: Sector-agnostic — HealthTech, FinTech, Green Energy, AI/ML, Consumer Tech
Notes: Jaipur (legal name Real Time Accelerator LLP). Founded 2020 (2022-vintage fund). SEBI-registered angel fund. GP Amit Singal; GP Dr Vibhuti Aggarwal; IC member Sandeep Bansal. 750+ angel investor community; 34–40+ startups. Runs a curated accelerator (seed–pre-series). Portfolio: MentorKart, MyWays.ai, MyMandi, Stylox, Innoctive, Pantherun (Series A $12M), Burgerama, CargoFL. Ticket researched: typical ticket ~₹1 Cr (VCCircle launch); Seedleap accelerator up to ₹2 Cr (IIF Leaders Speak / RTAF).
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): RealTime — formally the Real Time Angel Fund (RTAF), operating through Real Time Accelerator LLP — is a SEBI-registered angel fund based in Jaipur, founded in 2020 and led by General Partner Amit Singal alongside General Partner Dr. Vibhuti Aggarwal and investment-committee member Sandeep Bansal. Its mission is to collaborate with 'future change-makers' to build and scale impact startups, and it pairs capital with a curated accelerator program designed specifically for seed to pre-series companies, layering in mentorship and operational support. RTAF is sector-agnostic with a focus on healthtech, fintech, green energy, artificial intelligence and consumer technology, and typically writes cheques of ₹1–2 crore per startup at pre-seed, seed and pre-Series A. The fund has built a community of more than 750 angel investors and has backed over 34–40 startups, often serving founders building from 'Bharat to the world', including those in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. Its portfolio includes career-tech platform MentorKart, AI HR-tech startup MyWays.ai, B2B agri-marketplace MyMandi, fashion app Stylox, Innoctive, logistics firm CargoFL and food brand Burgerama; notably, portfolio company Pantherun Technologies went on to raise a $12 million Series A in late 2025. Beyond funding, RTAF emphasises active mentorship, ecosystem connections and follow-on fundraising support for its founders.

Company Thesis: Back profitable, product-market-fit growth-stage tech companies expanding via overseas expansion, inorganic acquisition, tech-team and CXO hiring or pre-IPO scaling; a research- and data-driven, hands-on partnership model. India's first 'Pro Rata' fund, accessing oversubscribed rounds of top tech companies alongside top-tier growth funds.
Sector: Consumer Internet, SaaS, B2B Platforms, FinTech (sector-agnostic tech)
Notes: Bengaluru. Founded 2022 by Navin Honagudi (ex-Kae Capital partner, 10+ yrs; 50+ investments incl Paytm/Shiprocket/Vedantu) & Abhisekh Shah. $200M fund (debut close ~$160M), SEBI Cat-II AIF + green-shoe; 12–14 investments planned. Anchored by KB Investment (South Korea's KB Group, ~$100M / 20%). Institutionally backed by Venture Catalysts (VCats group's 4th fund). Portfolio: smallcase, IDfy, AstroTalk (INR 110 Cr), Snapmint; exits incl. BluSmart, ReshaMandi.
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Elev8 Venture Partners is a Bengaluru-based, growth-stage venture firm founded in 2022 and led by co-founder and Managing Director Navin Honagudi, who previously spent over a decade as a partner at Kae Capital, where he invested in 50-plus companies including Paytm, Shiprocket and Vedantu. Elev8 runs a $200 million India-focused, sector-agnostic fund (with a debut close around $160 million), licensed as a SEBI Category-II AIF with a green-shoe option, and concentrates on Series B and C rounds in profitable, technology-driven companies that have established product-market fit and are scaling — whether for overseas expansion, inorganic acquisitions, technology-team and CXO hiring, or positioning for an eventual IPO. Ticket sizes run $5–15 million across a focused portfolio of roughly 12–14 companies, spanning consumer internet, SaaS, B2B platforms and fintech, and the firm describes itself as India's first 'Pro Rata' fund, accessing oversubscribed rounds alongside top-tier growth investors via proprietary data-driven algorithms. Elev8 is anchored by South Korea's KB Investment (part of KB Group), which committed around $100 million and supports Southeast Asia expansion, and is institutionally backed by early-stage platform Venture Catalysts. Its portfolio includes smallcase, identity-verification firm IDfy, spiritual-tech platform AstroTalk and no-credit-card EMI provider Snapmint, with the broader team's track record including exits such as BluSmart and ReshaMandi.

Company Thesis: 'Destination Accelerator' — a fund-led, multi-stage accelerator helping startups at every stage through a rigorous, methodical cohort program across eight industry-specialised verticals, leveraging local industry, academia, legal/compliance and resource support to drive growth and impact.
Sector: Sector-agnostic (eight specialised verticals incl. FinTech, HealthTech, Enterprise, Consumer)
Cheque Size: Pre-seed/seed cohort investment + follow-on; Cohort '25 offered up to $10M funding support
Notes: Gurugram. Founded 2017. India's leading fund-led accelerator; first Indian member of the Global Accelerator Network (GAN); Best Accelerator 2021 (Startup India awards). Runs own SEBI Cat-I & Cat-II funds + a GIFT City fund; later-stage investing via Finvolve. 98–120+ startups; combined onboarded valuation $253M+; 12 partial exits; 5,600+ jobs created. Programs incl. Sanjeevan Healthcare (with i-Hub Gujarat) and TomorrowLAB (Tata Steel + IIT Bhubaneswar).
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): India Accelerator (IA) is a Gurugram-based, fund-led, multi-stage startup accelerator — among the most active in the country and the first Indian program to be affiliated with the Global Accelerator Network (GAN), recognised as Best Accelerator 2021 at the Startup India awards. Built around a thesis it calls 'Destination Accelerator', IA runs a rigorous, methodical cohort program that is sector-agnostic but organised into eight industry-specialised verticals, each led by subject-matter experts and an investment committee that reviews, mentors and connects startups for growth. A key differentiator is that IA backs its cohorts with its own capital: it operates SEBI Category-I and Category-II funds and a GIFT City fund, and invests in comparatively later-stage businesses through its arm Finvolve, creating an ecosystem (its 'multiverse') designed to support companies at every stage with mentorship, market access, legal/compliance help and follow-on funding. Over recent years IA has supported more than 98–120 startups, with onboarded companies carrying a combined valuation exceeding $253 million, 12 partial exits and over 5,600 jobs created. It also runs targeted programs in partnership with institutions and corporates — including the Sanjeevan Healthcare Accelerator with i-Hub Gujarat and TomorrowLAB with Tata Steel and IIT Bhubaneswar — and unveiled a Cohort '25 offering up to $10 million in funding support.

Company Type: Angel Fund → Micro VC (SEBI AIF) [rebranded 'Enlighten Capital', Dec 2024]
Company Thesis: Support early-stage founders building disruptive solutions in emerging technologies aligned with India's innovation and sustainable-development vision; a structured investment approach backed by a strong network of LPs and angels, aimed at addressing the critical early-stage funding gap.
Sector: Emerging Technologies, Smart Manufacturing, Mobility, FinTech
Cheque Size: Micro-VC early-stage cheques (Fund 1 INR 100 Cr + INR 100 Cr greenshoe = INR 200 Cr)
Notes: Chennai. Founded 2022 as Enlighten Angel Fund (EnlightenVC.online). Rebranded to Enlighten Capital (full-fledged Micro VC) in Dec 2024 after receiving SEBI AIF approval. Maiden fund: INR 100 Cr raised from LPs + INR 100 Cr greenshoe (INR 200 Cr target). GPs Koushik Shekar (ex-Sutherland, Citi) & Arvind Subramaniam; partners Goutham Sekhar, Snehali Mansingh Khamkar, Rohit Mohan; team ~7. Syndicated 10+ investments as an angel fund. Runs the iZentral startup carnival (with Startup India, i-Hub Gujarat).
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Enlighten Angel Fund — now rebranded as Enlighten Capital — is a Chennai-based early-stage investor founded in 2022 that, over its first two years, operated as an angel fund and syndicated more than ten investments while building a reputation for identifying and nurturing high-potential ventures. In early December 2024 it received SEBI approval to operate as an Alternative Investment Fund and rebranded into a full-fledged micro-VC, completing a ₹100 crore maiden fund (Fund 1) raised from limited partners and launching fundraising for an additional ₹100 crore greenshoe option, taking its target corpus to ₹200 crore. The fund focuses on early-stage, disruptive startups in sectors it sees as driving change — emerging technologies, smart manufacturing, mobility and fintech — explicitly aligning its thesis with India's vision for innovation and sustainable development. Enlighten is led by General Partners Koushik Shekar, who moved from technology roles at Sutherland and Citi into consulting and angel investing, and Arvind Subramaniam, an entrepreneur and operator, supported by a partner team of Goutham Sekhar, Snehali Mansingh Khamkar and Rohit Mohan. Backed by a structured investment approach and a strong network of LPs and angels, the fund positions itself as an institutional enabler addressing the critical early-stage funding gap, and runs ecosystem initiatives such as its iZentral startup carnival.

Invests in(Preseed, Seed, Series A ...): Pre-Seed, Seed (up to Series B via fund)
Company Thesis: Founders-first, community-based investment platform connecting founders, angels, operators and global funds; give early-stage entrepreneurs funding visibility plus active mentoring and business support, with strong reach into Tier 2/3/4 cities and women founders. Backs founders on knowledge, experience, passion and attitude.
Sector: Sector-agnostic (EV, D2C, SaaS, Robotics, FinTech, AR/VR, AgriTech, HealthTech, EdTech)
Cheque Size: $300K–$1M (EvolveX provides $20–30K seed + helps raise up to $100K)
Notes: Founded Aug 2020 (Surat/Delhi). 13,000+ angel community across 80+ countries. Co-founders: Neeraj Tyagi (CEO; passed away Aug 18, 2025), Gaurav VK Singhvi, Bhawna Bhatnagar, Vikas Aggarwal, Deo Saurabh; team ~24–63 incl ~8 partners. Vehicles: EvolveX accelerator, Invstt.com platform, Avinya Ventures (VC fund), Invstt Trust (SEBI angel fund) + GIFT City fund. 134–162 startups, 200+ deals; 1 IPO (TradeUNO), 1 acquisition (Flatheads); 10x exit in OLL. 33% Tier 2/3, ~27% female founders. Portfolio: Pandorum, Zypp Electric, Stage OTT, ScrapUncle, Oben Electric, Anveshan, Garuda Aerospace.
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): We Founder Circle (WFC) is a founders-led, community-based startup investment platform established in August 2020 that has grown into one of India's largest angel networks, with a community of more than 13,000 angels spanning over 80 countries. Built on a founders-first thesis — evaluating ventures on knowledge, experience, passion and attitude — WFC gives early-stage entrepreneurs both funding visibility and active mentoring, with a notable focus on Tier 2/3/4 cities (around a third of its portfolio) and women founders (close to 30%). The platform operates a full stack of vehicles: the EvolveX global accelerator, which provides pre-seed startups roughly $20–30K and helps them raise up to $100,000; the Invstt.com community and marketplace platform; a dedicated VC fund, Avinya Ventures; and regulated structures including a SEBI angel fund (Invstt Trust) and a GIFT City fund for global investors. Across these, WFC typically backs companies from seed to Series B with $300K–$1M cheques, sector-agnostically across EV, D2C, SaaS, robotics, fintech, agritech and more. It has invested in over 130 startups through 200-plus deals, producing an IPO (TradeUNO), an acquisition (Flatheads) and a 10x exit, with portfolio names including Zypp Electric, Oben Electric, Stage OTT, ScrapUncle, Anveshan and Garuda Aerospace. Co-founder and CEO Neeraj Tyagi, who led the firm, passed away in August 2025.

Company Thesis: Empower startups with connections, expertise and hands-on support — notably through its 'Scaleation' / 3rd Horizon Scaleators program — to help them navigate scaling challenges and build sustainable, steadily-growing companies.
Sector: Enterprise SaaS, Software Infrastructure, Consumer Services, FinTech, Healthcare, Future of Work, Real Estate/Construction Tech, AI applications
Notes: Ahmedabad. Founded 2022. Small team of ~8 (1 partner + 7 venture partners; India & Romania). Runs the '3rd Horizon Scaleators' / Scaleation program for growth-stage startups. Few disclosed investments: agprop (led seed, 2023), SR Charging Stations (EV charging), Varistor Technologies. Limited public data on fund size and cheque size.
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Kathyawad Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm based in Ahmedabad, founded in 2022, that focuses on seed-stage investments in Indian startups while emphasising hands-on scaling support. A distinctive feature is its 'Scaleation' / 3rd Horizon Scaleators program — a structured 'scaleator' designed specifically for growth-stage startups navigating the difficult journey from problem identification and ideation through market entry and scale, where the firm provides connections, domain expertise and operational guidance. Backed by what it describes as a decade of financial expertise, Kathyawad concentrates on sectors including enterprise SaaS, software infrastructure, consumer services, fintech, healthcare, the future of work, and real estate and construction tech, with a stated emphasis on building sustainable companies. Its team of around eight spans a partner and several venture partners across India and Romania. Public disclosure on the firm is limited — its fund size and typical cheque size are not published, and only a handful of investments are on record, including agtech/proptech startup agprop (a seed round it led in 2023), EV-charging network SR Charging Stations and clean-energy/fire-safety firm Varistor Technologies — so this profile is intentionally conservative pending further confirmation.

Company Type: Accelerator VC fund (idea/early-stage; flagship fund of Venture Catalysts Group)
Company Thesis: Be the 'Y Combinator of India' — provide initial capital plus committed follow-on to idea-stage startups, supporting them across their first three funding rounds before connecting them to large VCs for growth capital.
Sector: Stage & sector-agnostic (Robotics, Healthcare, EV, Defence, D2C, SaaS, Travel, FinTech, DeepTech, Media, InsurTech, Logistics)
Cheque Size: First cheque $250K–$300K (~60% of corpus); follow-on up to $3M
Notes: Mumbai. Founded 2020 as 9Unicorns; rebranded to 100Unicorns in 2024. Flagship accelerator-VC fund of Venture Catalysts Group. Co-founders Apoorva Ranjan Sharma (MD), Gaurav Jain, Anil Jain, Anuj Golecha. Fund I $100M (140–185 startups, ~9 exits); Fund II $200M + $100M green-shoe (target 200 startups), with UAE/ADGM presence; ~15% allocated to US/MENA/Africa/Asia. Portfolio: VideoVerse, Zypp Electric, Renee Cosmetics, Trunativ, IGP, LiquiLoans, ImpactGuru.
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): 100Unicorns — formerly 9Unicorns — is a Mumbai-based accelerator venture capital fund founded in 2020 as the flagship early-stage vehicle of the Venture Catalysts Group, and is often described as India's first accelerator VC. Co-founded by Apoorva Ranjan Sharma (also Managing Director of Venture Catalysts) along with Gaurav Jain, Anil Jain and Anuj Golecha, its explicit ambition is to become 'the Y Combinator of India', backing promising founders right from the ideation stage with initial capital plus committed follow-on, and supporting them across their first three funding rounds before connecting them to larger VCs for growth capital. Its first fund closed at $100 million and invested in more than 140 startups across fintech, deeptech, enterprise SaaS, media, insurtech and D2C, producing several category leaders and around nine exits. In 2024 the firm rebranded to 100Unicorns and launched a second fund targeting $200 million with a $100 million green-shoe, aiming to back 200 early-stage startups; roughly 60% of the corpus funds first cheques of $250K–$300K with follow-ons up to $3 million, and about 15% is earmarked for startups in the US, Middle East, Africa and Asia, supported by a new ADGM presence in the UAE. Portfolio names include VideoVerse, Zypp Electric, Renee Cosmetics, Trunativ, IGP, LiquiLoans and ImpactGuru.

Company Thesis: Operate as a Corporate Venture Capital arm that backs and builds acquisitions to disrupt industries and improve lives — dedicating resources and specialised teams to 'architect the NEXT Stars'; occasionally co-invests with like-minded investors.
Sector: Multi-sector / sector-agnostic (roots in Datacenters & Software Services)
Notes: Mumbai. Founded 2018. Small team of ~3 (2 partners + 1 principal). Operates as a Corporate Venture Capital (CVC); grew out of a founder group that built datacenter and software-services companies with 2,000+ employees. Limited public disclosure on fund size, cheque size and portfolio. (Distinct from Sorin Investment Mgmt, Next Orbit Ventures and Nu Ventures, which are unrelated.)
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Next Star Venture Capital LLP is a Mumbai-based investment firm founded in 2018 that operates primarily as a Corporate Venture Capital (CVC) vehicle. According to the firm, its journey began as a startup that created companies spanning datacenters and software services, growing to over 2,000 employees, and it now channels that operating experience into venture investing — backing and building acquisitions that aim to disrupt industries and improve lives, while dedicating teams and resources to 'architect the NEXT Stars'. It occasionally invites like-minded co-investors into its deals. The firm is small and sector-agnostic, run by a compact team of around three (two partners and a principal). Public disclosure is very limited: its fund size, typical cheque size and a named portfolio are not publicly available, and it should not be confused with similarly named but unrelated firms such as Sorin Investment Management, Next Orbit Ventures or Nu Ventures. This profile is therefore intentionally conservative and would benefit from primary confirmation of strategy and track record.

Company Type: Micro-VC (early-stage; multi-stage platform via Artha India Ventures family office)
Invests in(Preseed, Seed, Series A ...): Seed, Pre-Series A, Series A (+ Series B/C follow-on via Artha Select Fund)
Company Thesis: Pioneer of India's micro-VC model — back tech-enabled (not tech-first) 'category creators' from day zero, combining early-stage experience, operator insight, family-office networks and institutional discipline; concentrate capital on winners via a proprietary '1–2–4' escalating follow-on model.
Sector: Premium Consumption, FinTech Infrastructure, Applied AI, DeepTech, D2C & D2C enablers, B2B
Cheque Size: AVF II: INR 4 Cr initial + INR 8–16 Cr follow-on (targets 15–20% ownership); Artha Select ~$2.3–2.5M Series B/C
Notes: Mumbai. India's first early-stage micro-VC. MP Anirudh A. Damani (2nd-gen investor, 4th-gen entrepreneur). Backed by Artha India Ventures (family office of Ashok Kumar & Ramesh Damani) + Singularity Ventures (Madhusudan Kela). AVF I INR 225 Cr (final close 2021), 32 seed startups, 61% IRR; Artha Select Fund (winners-only) final close INR 432 Cr/$49.4M (2025); AVF II INR 500 Cr target (INR 250 Cr first close Oct 2025) + INR 100 Cr green-shoe, 36 seed startups. Platform AUM ~INR 2,100–2,300 Cr; 130–140 cos since 2012. Portfolio: OYO, Rapido, Purplle, Everest Fleet, Agnikul Cosmos, InstaAstro.
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Artha Venture Fund (AVF) is a Mumbai-based, early-stage micro-VC widely regarded as a pioneer of India's micro-venture model, led by Managing Partner Anirudh A. Damani — a second-generation investor and fourth-generation entrepreneur — and backed by Artha India Ventures, the family office of Ashok Kumar and Ramesh Damani, alongside Madhusudan Kela's Singularity Ventures. Artha backs tech-enabled (deliberately not 'tech-first') category creators from day zero, combining operator insight, family-office networks and institutional discipline, and concentrates capital on winners through a proprietary '1–2–4' escalating follow-on model. Its debut fund (AVF I), a roughly ₹225 crore Category-I AIF closed in 2021, deployed across 32 seed-stage startups and has reported a 61% IRR with portfolio valuation exceeding ₹750 crore and FY25 portfolio revenues over ₹2,100 crore. A 'winners-only' follow-on vehicle, the Artha Select Fund, closed at about ₹432 crore ($49 million) in 2025 to back the top 15% of its portfolio in Series B/C rounds. In October 2025 Artha announced the first close (₹250 crore) of Artha Venture Fund II, targeting ₹500 crore plus a ₹100 crore green-shoe to back 36 seed-stage startups across premium consumption, fintech infrastructure, applied AI and deeptech, with ₹4 crore initial cheques. Across its platform — managing roughly ₹2,100–2,300 crore — Artha has backed 130-plus companies including OYO, Rapido, Purplle, Everest Fleet and Agnikul Cosmos.

Company Type: Proprietary Venture Fund + Fund-of-Funds / Family Office (multi-asset)
Company Thesis: Build an expansive, India-centric platform of investment opportunities — make direct investments in technology-driven businesses with large India-first market potential, while seeding and anchoring entrepreneurial fund managers as a prime LP to broaden access to the startup ecosystem and keep companies domiciled in India.
Sector: Life Sciences, Healthcare, Education (+ Climate Tech, AgriTech, Consumer, Software)
Cheque Size: Direct early/growth cheques; ~$150M proprietary fund (~$450M ecosystem across funds)
Notes: Bengaluru. Founded ~2011 by T.V. Mohandas Pai (ex-Infosys CFO/board) & Dr. Ranjan Pai (Manipal Education & Medical Group) — the two are not related. MD Deepak Natraj. ~$150M proprietary fund + Fund-of-Funds; seeded/anchored 10+ funds (3one4 Capital, Exfinity Venture Partners, Ideaspring, Saha Fund) as prime LP. ~$450M ecosystem, 266 investments, 35 independent fund managers. Portfolio/exits: Byju's, PharmEasy (API Holdings), HomeLane, ZoomCar, Licious, Kapiva, Faircent, 88academics.
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Aarin Capital is a Bengaluru-based proprietary venture fund and fund-of-funds, co-founded around 2011 by T.V. Mohandas Pai — the former CFO and board member of Infosys and a Padma Shri awardee — and Dr. Ranjan Pai, chairman of the Manipal Education and Medical Group (the two share a surname but are not related). Structured partly as a family office spanning multiple asset classes, Aarin makes direct investments in startups while also acting as a prime limited partner across 10-to-15-plus funds covering early- and growth-stage venture capital, public markets, real estate project financing, hedge funds and private equity. Its direct thesis centres on technology-driven businesses in life sciences, healthcare and education with large, India-centric or India-first market opportunities, and it has progressively expanded into impact areas such as climate tech and agritech. A distinctive feature is its role as an ecosystem builder: Aarin has helped launch and seed funds including 3one4 Capital, Exfinity Venture Partners, Ideaspring Capital and Saha Fund, where the Pais serve as both GPs and LPs, supported by around 35 independent fund managers across a roughly $450 million ecosystem. Its direct portfolio and exits include Byju's, PharmEasy, HomeLane, ZoomCar, Licious, Kapiva and Faircent. The firm explicitly works to keep promising Indian companies domiciled in India.

Company Type: Global Investment Firm / Family Office (multi-asset: public equity, PE, growth VC)
Invests in(Preseed, Seed, Series A ...): Growth-stage VC, Private Equity, Public Equity (long-term)
Company Thesis: Be a globally-respected catalyst that converts the ideas of passionate, skilled, value-driven entrepreneurs into tangible business outcomes; a long-term investor that prizes relationships, corporate governance and sustainable value creation across stages.
Sector: Multi-sector — Technology, E-commerce, FinTech, Consumer, Healthcare, Education, DeepTech, Precision Manufacturing
Cheque Size: Growth/PE cheques (>$1B AUM across asset classes)
Notes: Bengaluru. Founded 2009 by N.R. Narayana Murthy (Infosys founder); manages the assets of the Murthy family. >$1B AUM across public equity, PE and growth VC. President Deepak Padaki; Chairman MD Ranganath (ex-Infosys CFO). Original Catamaran Venture Fund ~INR 600 Cr; first deal SKS Microfinance (2010). ~37 investments, 3 exits. Portfolio: SpaceX, udaan, Udemy, Acko, Log 9, Manipal Health. Distinct from Catamaran Ventures UK (Akshata Murty's, winding down).
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Catamaran is a Bengaluru-based global investment firm and family office established in 2009 by N.R. Narayana Murthy, the founder of Infosys, to manage the assets of Murthy and his family. Managing over $1 billion across asset classes — spanning public equity, private equity and growth-stage venture capital — Catamaran describes its purpose as being a catalyst that converts the ideas of passionate, skilled and value-driven entrepreneurs into tangible business outcomes, and it positions itself as a patient, long-term investor that prizes relationships, corporate governance and sustainable value creation. Its original venture vehicle, the roughly ₹600 crore Catamaran Venture Fund, made its first investment in SKS Microfinance and initially targeted healthcare, education and nutrition; over time the platform has built a diverse portfolio that includes SpaceX, deep-tech energy startup Log 9, B2B e-commerce leader udaan, edtech firm Udemy and fintech player Acko, among around 37 investments. Led by President Deepak Padaki and Chairman M.D. Ranganath (a former Infosys CFO), Catamaran has more recently signalled a focus on services and precision manufacturing — backing startups capable of exporting deep-tech and automotive components as India attracts manufacturing investment. It is a separate entity from the now-winding-down UK-based Catamaran Ventures associated with Akshata Murty, with no investment overlap between the two.

Company Type: Single Family Office (Kris Gopalakrishnan family) — SEBI Cat-II AIF + FoF
Invests in(Preseed, Seed, Series A ...): Late-stage (debt & equity) + LP in VC/PE/debt funds across stages
Company Thesis: Support entrepreneurship, technological advances and scientific research in India; back growth/late-stage startups with great founders, strong products and high standards of corporate governance, co-investing alongside leading institutional investors with a similar long-term approach.
Notes: Bengaluru. Founded 2014/2015. Single family office / private investment arm of Kris Gopalakrishnan (Infosys co-founder; Padma Bhushan; chairman of Axilor Ventures). Managed via Prayog Advisors LLP; runs the Pratithi Investment Fund (SEBI Cat-II AIF). 100+ startups (81 India, 6 US), 7 unicorns (Yubi, Uniphore, XpressBees). Recent deals: Planys Technologies, Agnikul, JetSynthesys. Related family entities: Pratiksha Trust (R&D/innovation philanthropy with IISc, IIT Madras), SGK Trust (real estate). Ticket researched: $4M–$10M (India VC / family office directories).
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Pratithi Investments is the single family office and private investment arm of the Kris Gopalakrishnan family, founded around 2014-15 and based in Bengaluru. Kris Gopalakrishnan is a co-founder of Infosys, a Padma Bhushan awardee and chairman of the Axilor Ventures accelerator, and Pratithi reflects his conviction that the nation's growth will be fuelled by the innovation and enterprise of its people. Administered through Prayog Advisors LLP and investing via the SEBI Category-II Pratithi Investment Fund, the firm's mission is to support entrepreneurship, technological advances and scientific research in India. It is sector-agnostic and primarily backs growth and late-stage startups — across both debt and equity — while also committing as a limited partner to venture capital, private equity and debt funds across stages. Its investment approach centres on the quality of the founding team, the scale of the opportunity and a high standard of corporate governance, and it typically co-invests alongside leading institutional investors. Since launching, Pratithi has backed over a hundred startups across sectors, including seven unicorns such as Yubi, Uniphore and XpressBees, with recent participation in deep-tech and space names like Planys Technologies and Agnikul. The broader family platform also encompasses the Pratiksha Trust, which funds R&D and innovation in brain science and computing at institutions such as IISc and IIT Madras.

Company Type: Single Family Office (impact; Gogri family / Aarti Industries) — for-profit + not-for-profit pools
Company Thesis: Solve large-scale societal problems with novel solutions; allocate for-profit and not-for-profit pools of capital to optimise financial, societal and environmental returns — backing technologies and businesses that aim to arrest and reverse climate change, alongside organisations making health and education more accessible and affordable.
Sector: Climate Tech, DeepTech, Environment Tech, Clean Energy, Sustainable Agriculture, Alternate Materials, Health, Education, FinTech
Notes: Mumbai. Founded 2021. Single family office of Rajendra & Arti Gogri (promoters of Aarti Industries Ltd, specialty chemicals). Two capital pools (for-profit + not-for-profit). 51 portfolio cos (~5 new/yr); team 6 incl 2 partners; 1 acquisition. Portfolio: Atomberg, Miko Technologies, Cityflo, Blue Sky Analytics, EEKI Foods, Ashaya, Polycycl, Kreedo, Volt14, MOOEV. Co-invests with Blume, Omnivore, Inflection Point Ventures. (Distinct from the US impact-investing consultancy 'Spectrum Impact' run by Rehana Nathoo.)
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Spectrum Impact is a Mumbai-based single family office founded in 2021 to manage the assets and investments of Rajendra and Arti Gogri, promoters of Aarti Industries Limited, a leading Indian specialty-chemicals company. The firm is committed to solving large-scale societal problems with novel solutions, and operates two distinct pools of capital — a proprietary for-profit pool and a separate not-for-profit pool — allocating across both to optimise financial, societal and environmental returns simultaneously. Its core focus is backing technologies and businesses that aim to arrest and reverse climate change, alongside organisations working to make health and education more accessible and affordable. Reflecting this, its portfolio spans climate tech, deep tech, clean energy, sustainable agriculture, alternate materials, health and education. Spectrum invests primarily at the seed and early stage and has built a portfolio of around 51 companies, supported by a small team of about six including two partners. Notable investments include energy-efficient-appliance maker Atomberg, robotics firm Miko Technologies, urban-mobility company Cityflo, geospatial-data startup Blue Sky Analytics, hydroponics venture EEKI Foods, waste-innovation enterprise Ashaya, plastic-recycling firm Polycycl and battery-tech startup Volt14, frequently co-investing with funds such as Blume Ventures, Omnivore and Inflection Point Ventures. It should not be confused with the unrelated US impact-investing consultancy of the same name.

Company Type: Single Family Office (GVK / G V Sanjay Reddy family) — investment, growth & philanthropic platform
Invests in(Preseed, Seed, Series A ...): Early to growth-stage (via Reddy Futures Fund; pure-play co-investing)
Company Thesis: Back far-sighted entrepreneurial teams and take strategic equity positions in category-defining tech companies, while incubating its own businesses; invest across 'private exponentials (technology), public compounders (equities) and fundamentals'; bring new technologies to India and take transformative Indian innovations to the world. Purpose: 'Enabling Ideas that change the world.'
Sector: FinTech, Commerce/Shopping, EdTech, Community/Lifestyle, Design, Technology
Cheque Size: Co-invests alongside leading global angels & VCs (family-office cheques)
Notes: Hyderabad. Founded 2015 (formerly Keshav Reddy Family Office); the investment/growth/philanthropic platform of the G V Sanjay Reddy family (GVK Group). Runs the Reddy Futures Fund — a pure-play fund co-investing with top global angels/VCs. Led by GV Sanjay Reddy & Pinky Reddy; Keshav Reddy (MBA MIT, BSE Michigan; ex-VP GVK Airports; founder of Equal) runs the fund. ~22–30 investments, 5–6 unicorns: CRED, Upstox, Khatabook, Chipper Cash, Hive (Hive AI), Genies. Philanthropy: Pinky & Sanjay Reddy Foundation (education/healthcare); GVK EMRI (world's largest free ambulance service — 15,000 ambulances).
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Reddy Ventures is the investment, growth and philanthropic platform of the G V Sanjay Reddy family — part of the GVK Group — headquartered in Hyderabad and founded in 2015 (formerly the Keshav Reddy Family Office). The family began treating startups as a distinct asset class through its Reddy Futures Fund, a 'pure-play' vehicle that invests alongside some of the best angel investors and VCs globally in technology startups, complementing the family's existing allocations to real estate, public equities, bonds and group companies. The fund is run by Keshav Reddy — an MIT MBA and former Vice President at GVK Airports, founder of digital-identity startup Equal, and a board member of Aragen Life Sciences and GVK EMRI — while GV Sanjay Reddy and Pinky Reddy lead the broader platform. As active, hands-on partners, Reddy Ventures takes meaningful stakes and offers mentorship and resources across sectors such as fintech, commerce, edtech, community and lifestyle, and design. Its portfolio of roughly 30 investments includes five to six unicorns — CRED, Upstox, Khatabook, Chipper Cash, Hive (Hive AI) and Genies. The family is also deeply philanthropic: Pinky Reddy leads foundation work in education and healthcare, and the family-owned GVK EMRI operates the world's largest free ambulance service, with a fleet of around 15,000 ambulances serving hundreds of millions across India.

Company Thesis: A sector-agnostic, Gen Z-centric, 'India Only' early-stage fund backing young and first-time Indian founders building uniquely Indian companies for the 'New India' opportunity; acts as a hyperlocal bridge connecting global investors with Indian founders, prioritising speed, transparency and founder-friendliness, and leads over half of its deals.
Sector: Consumer Tech, FinTech, Food & Beverage, AI, Global SaaS (sector-agnostic)
Notes: Offices in Mumbai, Bengaluru, Delhi NCR and Los Angeles. Founded 2021 by Founding Partners Hershel Mehta & Brendan Rogers (co-founder of Wag!, NASDAQ: PET). Fund I $10M, ~47–48 startups; Fund II (2025) targets up to 30 startups, pre-seed to seed. 54–59 portfolio cos, 1 unicorn (Zepto), 3 acquisitions (Krave Mart, Coolberg). Portfolio: NEWME, Apna Mart, Bimaplan, Karbon Card, Blitzllama, Procureyard, inframandi, Fibr, Intervue. Co-invests with Titan Capital, 3one4, Y Combinator, Orios, India Quotient, 100X.VC. | Ticket researched: Typical check $100K–$500K (indianvcs.com / VenturLoop)
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): 2am VC is an early-stage, India-focused venture firm founded in 2021 by Founding Partners Hershel Mehta and Brendan Rogers (the latter also a co-founder of Nasdaq-listed Wag!), with offices across Mumbai, Bengaluru, Delhi NCR and Los Angeles. The firm describes itself as a sector-agnostic, Gen Z-centric, 'India Only' fund, built on the conviction that the next stage of India's startup development will be driven by young and first-time founders building uniquely Indian companies — what it calls the 'New India' opportunity. Blending Indian and international perspectives, 2am VC positions itself as a hyperlocal partner that bridges global investors and Indian founders, emphasising speed, transparency, founder-friendliness and cross-border synergies, and it aims to lead more than half of its deals, investing via iSAFE, SAFE, convertible notes and priced rounds. Its $10 million debut fund backed around 47 companies; in 2025 it launched Fund II to invest in up to 30 startups predominantly at pre-seed to seed across consumer tech, fintech, food and beverage, AI and global SaaS, reserving 60% for initial cheques and 40% for follow-ons. Across roughly 54–59 portfolio companies — including NEWME, Apna Mart, Bimaplan, Karbon Card, Fibr and Intervue — it counts one unicorn (Zepto) and three acquisitions.

Company Type: Investment firm (growth/PE + public equities; evergreen, India-focused)
Invests in(Preseed, Seed, Series A ...): Series A to IPO and beyond (multi-stage, private + public)
Company Thesis: Partner for the long term with some of India's most promising mid-sized companies — public or private — run by outstanding entrepreneurs and management teams; provide patient, purpose-driven capital via an evergreen structure, taking substantial (often minority) stakes, frequently second only to the founder, and holding for years or decades while helping companies succeed.
Sector: Sector-agnostic (Financial Services/FinTech, Consumer, SaaS, EdTech, Healthcare, Insurance)
Notes: India-focused, public + private markets; based across India and Silicon Valley. Founded 2000 (one of India's first VC funds); merged with Sequoia Capital to form Sequoia Capital India (2006); revived as an independent firm in 2011 when founders Sumir Chadha, KP Balaraj, Sandeep Singhal & SK Jain left Sequoia India. Evergreen fund; AUM crossed $7–10B+; raised a $1.5B crossover fund (2023). 132 companies (104 India startups), 8 unicorns, 19 soonicorns. Portfolio: PhysicsWallah, LeadSquared, Vedantu, LEAD, Star Health, India Shelter, Aptus, Rapido, Innovaccer; listed Axis Bank, Dr Lal PathLabs, Havells, Mindtree, IndiGo.
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): WestBridge Capital is an India-focused investment firm that invests across both public and private markets, with teams in India and Silicon Valley. Originally founded in 2000 as one of India's pioneering venture funds, it merged with Sequoia Capital in 2006 to form Sequoia Capital India; then in 2011 its founding managing directors — Sumir Chadha, K.P. Balaraj, Sandeep Singhal and S.K. Jain — separated the India-focused funds from Sequoia to re-establish WestBridge as an independent firm. WestBridge runs an evergreen, long-term, patient-capital model with assets under management that have crossed roughly $7–10 billion, and in 2023 it raised a $1.5 billion crossover fund, its largest-ever commitment for Indian companies. Its strategy is to partner with promising mid-sized businesses run by outstanding entrepreneurs — whether public or private — typically writing cheques of $25 million to $200 million for substantial, often minority, stakes (frequently second only to the founder) and holding for years or decades while taking board seats and providing operational support. Spanning Series A to IPO and beyond, its portfolio of around 132 companies includes eight unicorns such as PhysicsWallah, LeadSquared and Vedantu, plus listed names like Axis Bank, Dr Lal PathLabs, Havells, Mindtree and IndiGo, and newer bets including Star Health, India Shelter, Rapido and Innovaccer.

Company Thesis: Back ambitious founders building technology-driven businesses
Notes: Early-stage India-focused micro VC
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Aarii Ventures is an India-focused micro VC that backs ambitious founders at the earliest stages of company building. The firm is active at pre-seed and seed, writing cheques between $100k and $500k, positioning it as a meaningful first or co-lead institutional partner for founders who are just beginning to raise external capital. Aarii's sector interest spans SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, and D2C, reflecting a broad appetite for technology-driven business models with scalable unit economics. The firm's thesis centers on backing founders with strong conviction and a clear product vision, rather than requiring extensive traction at the point of investment. For Indian founders navigating the earliest and often most difficult stage of fundraising, Aarii Ventures represents the kind of early believer that can anchor a round and provide foundational credibility with later-stage investors. Founders building in the firm's focus sectors who are raising their first institutional round should consider Aarii as a relevant target, particularly if they are working on India-first problems with potential to scale. Reaching out through LinkedIn or the firm's website is the recommended approach for initial introductions.

Company Thesis: Invest in founders building scalable, tech-enabled businesses
Notes: Baheti family office; Jaipur-based
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Midas Capital is the investment arm of the Baheti family office, headquartered in Jaipur. The firm invests at Seed and Pre-Series A stages with cheque sizes ranging from $250k to $2M, making it a meaningful early institutional backer for Indian founders. Their focus spans SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, and D2C sectors, with a preference for businesses that leverage technology to build scalable, defensible models. Being a family office, Midas Capital typically offers founders a faster, more relationship-driven decision-making process compared to institutional VC funds, with flexibility on deal structuring. Founders can expect engagement from principals who have a long-term capital orientation and skin in the game beyond a fund cycle. Their Jaipur base also means they carry a practical, grounded perspective on India's non-metro consumer and business landscape, which can be an asset for founders targeting Bharat-centric markets. If you are raising your first or second institutional round and are building in their core sectors, Midas Capital is worth approaching with a crisp deck and early traction metrics.

Company Thesis: Back growth-oriented entrepreneurs building differentiated businesses
Notes: Ronnie Screwvala's investment fund; backed Upgrad, Ustraa
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Unilazer Ventures is the investment vehicle of Ronnie Screwvala, one of India's most respected entrepreneurs and the founder of UTV Group. The firm invests at Seed and Series A stages, with cheque sizes typically ranging from $500k to $5M, focusing on Consumer, D2C, FinTech, and HealthTech. What sets Unilazer apart is the value Ronnie personally brings beyond capital — deep brand-building instincts, a vast network across media, entertainment, and corporate India, and a genuine empathy for the founder journey having built and scaled businesses himself. Portfolio companies like upGrad and Ustraa reflect the firm's appetite for category-defining consumer businesses with strong brand DNA. Founders pitching to Unilazer should expect an engaged, hands-on relationship rather than a passive investor dynamic. The firm favors entrepreneurs who are building differentiated businesses with a clear path to scale, and who are not just chasing trends but are genuinely solving meaningful consumer needs. If you are an early-stage founder in a consumer-facing or digitally-enabled sector looking for a strategic partner with real operational credibility, Unilazer Ventures is worth a direct, well-prepared approach.

Company Thesis: Back founders who have a strong vision and ability to execute
Notes: India early-stage VC
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Hunch Ventures is an India-focused early-stage venture capital firm that partners with founders at the earliest and often most formative stages of their journey, from Pre-Seed through Pre-Series A. The firm's investment approach is firmly founder-first: the team looks for individuals who combine a compelling, differentiated vision with a demonstrated ability to execute against it, which is a combination that is especially critical in the competitive Indian startup landscape. Hunch Ventures invests across four core sectors, SaaS, Consumer, FinTech, and D2C, reflecting a belief that India's domestic demand story and digital infrastructure create durable tailwinds in each of these categories. Cheque sizes range from $100,000 to $1 million, making the firm a natural fit for founders who are raising their first institutional round or bridging toward a larger Series A. Founders approaching Hunch Ventures should be prepared to articulate not just a market opportunity but a clear-eyed plan for how they intend to build and scale their business. The firm's positioning at the earliest stages means it is comfortable with uncertainty but expects founders to bring conviction, domain insight, and a credible path forward.

Company Thesis: Partner with early-stage founders leveraging technology for scale
Notes: India-focused early stage micro VC
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Aroa Venture Partners is an India-focused micro VC operating at the pre-seed and seed stages, making it one of the earlier institutional checks a founder can receive. The firm writes cheques between $100,000 and $500,000, a range that suits founders who have a working hypothesis and early traction but are not yet ready for a large Series A institutional round. Their sector focus spans SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, and B2B, reflecting a broad interest in technology-enabled business models that can scale efficiently across Indian and global markets. The core philosophy is to partner with founders early, when the risk is highest but so is the potential to shape the company's direction meaningfully. For founders, this means Aroa is likely to be engaged beyond the cheque, offering support through the earliest and often most uncertain phases of company building. If you are a founder building in any of these sectors and are raising your first or second institutional round, Aroa Venture Partners is worth reaching out to early in your fundraising process before your round fills up.

Company Thesis: Invest in high-quality teams solving large market problems
Notes: Family office with active VC investing
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Aakash Emprise Pvt Ltd is an Indian family office that actively participates in early-stage venture investing, bridging the conviction-driven mindset of a family office with the hands-on engagement of a VC. The firm focuses on Seed and Pre-Series A rounds, deploying cheques in the $250k to $2M range, which positions it well to lead or co-lead early rounds for Indian startups. Their sector interest spans SaaS, FinTech, and Consumer, three of the most active verticals in the Indian startup ecosystem. The core investment philosophy centers on backing high-quality teams who are going after genuinely large market problems, suggesting that team quality and market size are weighted heavily in diligence conversations. For founders, this means demonstrating founder-market fit and a credible path to scale will likely resonate more than near-term revenue metrics alone. As a family office, Aakash Emprise can offer patient capital and decision-making that is often faster and less committee-driven than institutional funds, making them a practical option for founders seeking a collaborative early partner with meaningful cheque sizes.

Company Thesis: Back smart founders with bold ideas at the earliest stage
Notes: Aniruddha Malpani's investment vehicle; angel-first approach
Detailed Writeup (~200 words): Malpani Ventures is the investment vehicle of Dr. Aniruddha Malpani, one of India's most recognisable and outspoken angel investors. Operating at the pre-seed and seed stage, the firm backs founders before most institutional capital is willing to engage, making it a meaningful first cheque for early-stage companies. Cheque sizes typically range from $50,000 to $500,000, suitable for founders raising their first or second round. The firm has a broad sector mandate covering SaaS, FinTech, and consumer businesses, and does not restrict itself to a single vertical, which makes it accessible to a wide range of founding teams. Dr. Malpani is known in the Indian startup ecosystem for his directness, his commitment to founder education, and his willingness to engage even before a formal pitch. Founders who approach Malpani Ventures should come with a crisp articulation of the problem they are solving, a credible reason why they are the right team to solve it, and a genuine openness to feedback. The firm values intellectual honesty and long-term thinking over short-term vanity metrics. For founders at the earliest stage who want an experienced, engaged angel rather than a passive cheque, Malpani Ventures is worth a direct outreach.

Company Thesis: Invest in growth-stage technology companies in India
Notes: Growth-stage India-focused VC; founded by Siddharth Pai

Given the cheque size range, A100x typically participates in early rounds where it can add meaningful value beyond capital, including introductions, positioning advice, and follow-on support. Company Thesis: Invest in European and global deep tech companies

Company Thesis: Invest in B2B technology companies with global markets

For Indian B2B SaaS founders with US ambitions, Sierra Ventures represents one of the more accessible and contextually aware US institutional options.

Company Thesis: Back founders building technology companies with global potential from India

Company Thesis: Invest in data-driven founders building tech companies

Company Thesis: Back ambitious founders building scalable businesses in India

Company Thesis: Connect founders with impact-aligned capital and mentors

If your startup sits at the intersection of measurable social or environmental outcomes and scalable business models, SanchiConnect is worth engaging with early in your fundraising journey.

Company Thesis: Invest in businesses solving fundamental needs in India - food, health, energy and education

Company Thesis: Pioneer impact investing in India's most underserved communities

Company Thesis: Invest in AI-first startups building for global markets from India

Company Thesis: Founder-operator-led VC that makes few bets and stays deeply engaged; fast, decisive process with direct MP access; supports strategy, channel/client access and follow-on fundraise.

Company Thesis: Invest in founders building multiple category-defining businesses

Company Thesis: Invest in gaming, Web3 and FinTech founders at the earliest stage
Notes: Gullak, Fold, Koshance, Aura

Their portfolio includes Gullak, Fold, Koshance, and Aura, signalling a preference for founders building at the intersection of consumer behaviour and financial or digital infrastructure. For founders, Kira Studio is best approached when you have a strong thesis on your market and a clear sense of the problem you are solving, even if the product is still early. They are not a fit for late-stage rounds or sectors outside their core focus areas. Given their stage and cheque size, they are often a good first institutional name on a cap table, capable of opening doors to follow-on investors. Founders in gaming monetisation, DeFi applications, or consumer FinTech primitives are likely to find the strongest resonance with their investment perspective. Outreach is best made directly and concisely, with emphasis on the founding team's depth and the size of the opportunity being addressed.

Company Thesis: High-conviction fund backing 'category creators' — emerging founders building what the market doesn't yet have and solving meaningful India-centric problems; selective portfolio construction with hands-on, on-the-ground co-building.

Detailed Writeup (~200 words): WEH Ventures is a Mumbai-based, high-conviction early-stage venture fund founded in 2017 by Deepak Gupta, who moved from corporate bonds at Moody's and listed equity at Spark Capital into early-stage investing in 2015. The firm backs 'category creators' — emerging founders building products the market doesn't yet have and solving meaningful India-centric problems — and is known for selective portfolio construction and rolling up its sleeves to co-build alongside founders rather than simply providing capital. WEH typically invests at pre-seed and seed across fintech, consumer, content and entertainment, commerce, food, robotics and agritech, writing cheques of roughly INR 1–3 crore (about $120K–$400K) and pacing to around six deals a year while reserving close to 60% of each fund for follow-on rounds. Across three funds — its second sized at about INR 120 crore — it has made 30-plus investments. Its portfolio reads like a list of category pioneers: thematic-investing platform smallcase, micro-savings app Jar, street-food brand MasterChow, warehouse-robotics firm Unbox Robotics, Animall, Pratilipi and NOTO. In a notable milestone, WEH fully returned its debut fund in July 2025 through an exit from wealth-tech startup smallcase, a strong early validation of its conviction-led, category-creation thesis.

Company Thesis: Provide venture debt to high-growth startups in India

The fund works across sectors including SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, and D2C, and generally looks for startups that already have institutional equity investors on the cap table and demonstrate strong revenue momentum. Stride's portfolio includes well-known Indian consumer and tech brands, reflecting its comfort with businesses at various stages of maturity. For founders, Stride is a practical tool to bridge funding gaps, accelerate growth between Series A and Series B rounds, or complement an ongoing equity raise. Startups approaching Stride should come prepared with clear unit economics, a demonstrated repayment pathway, and ideally an existing institutional lead investor. The team is known for moving efficiently and understanding the operational realities of fast-scaling Indian startups.

Company Thesis: Invest in founders with the secret sauce to build great companies

Company Thesis: Invest in founders building tomorrow's most important companies today
